The 7 Best Firming Body Lotions for Tightening Skin, Tested by Experts

📅 2024-02-09  |  Read Source →

Editors gave top marks to formulas from Nivea and Charlotte Tilbury.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Skin changes are part of life—thanks to sun exposure, the natural dip in collagen and elastin once you hit your late 20s, or shifts in weight (hi, pregnancy!). So if your skin doesn’t quite have the same snap-back it once did, that’s completely normal. The good news? You don’t need pricey lasers or an intense 10-step routine to see a difference. The right body-firming lotion can help skin look plumper, smoother, and more resilient.

Firming body lotions can offer smoother, tighter, and less dimpled skin. While nothing can compare to the results you may get from an in-office procedure—topicals aren’t going to work miracles, after all—you might be surprised at just how far hydration can improve the appearance of crepey skin. “The physical transformation of hydration can be profound on our skin,” says dermatologist Nava Greenfield, MD. “The skin will actually appear plumper when a lotion used to ‘firm’ is applied. Adding nutrients to the skin on a consistent basis can also help in creating a healthy, firm appearance.”

Like other categories of skincare products, some firming formulas will always be better than others. To help streamline your shopping experience, I asked dermatologists for their expertise on how to shop for body lotions, along with product recommendations.

For the past few months, beauty contributor Danielle Blundell and I have been researching and testing the best firming lotions. After consulting six dermatologists for their shopping guidance, we asked for their no-fail recommendations as a starting point. We got our hands on some of these picks and shared our testing feedback to help you determine which option works for your unique beauty needs. And to ensure there was a variety of firming body lotions across all budgets, we spent hundreds of hours vetting products for their ingredient list, formulation, absorbency, long- and short-term hydration and firming benefits, and pricing. Of the dozens we tested, these were the best ones we’re willing to auto-refill.

So, get ready for smoother, tighter, and, yes, firmer skin.

Given the fast-acting results Blundell experienced, and the impressive ingredient list we knew the Nivea Skin Toning Gel-Cream was our best overall option. When looking at price, packaging size, and the strength of a given formula’s ingredients, this lightweight cream is hard to beat.

The combination of antioxidant Coenzyme Q10, which aids in cell turnover, and L-carnitine, a chemical known to bolster skin energy reserves and oxygen consumption in skin cells, packs a firming and hydrating punch that’ll leave your skin feeling silky-smooth. We saw improved tightness in just two weeks with twice daily use, and you can choose between almond and lotus scents depending on your preferences for fragrances.

Blundell loves the gel-like texture of this one—it’s a little bit runny right out of the tube, but it sinks into her skin with minimal rubbing and goes on with a bit of a cooling sensation, which feels especially refreshing in the mornings before work and during any waterfront vacations you’re taking. Hours after a quick application (and even a SoulCycle class and quick shower later), Blundell’s legs looked slightly more taut and still felt supple to the touch, as though she had just put the lotion on.

Sometimes the best products are the ones you’ll use religiously. To that end, you can slather on this lotion morning, noon, and night, thanks to its under $10 price tag and light-but-creamy texture that’s easy to apply. Blundell saw results like immediate hydration, but it took three weeks to notice less crepey skin.

“Although the role of topical collagen isn't fully understood yet, this product contains a hydrating form of vitamin B3, niacinamide, and a form of B5 panthenol, which strengthen skin and improve skin quality,” says Dr. Nazarian. “It also absorbs really nicely and applies easily and quickly, making it a great and affordable option for improving skin health.”

Dr. Sartor mentions the lotion does include a nice mix of moisturizers (petrolatum, stearic acid) to prevent water loss as well as antioxidants (niacinamide, tocopheryl acetate) for firming benefits, especially for its cost. “It also contains free fatty acids (palmitic acid) to repair the skin barrier,” she adds.

The only downside for the price? The formula contains a synthetic fragrance, so if you have sensitive skin, you might want to skip it for that reason.

Why settle for just skin firming on your body when you enjoy it on your face as well? This 2-in-1 lotion earned major snaps from dermatologist Dr. Lauren Penzi, MD, for that reason. "It has a powerful retinol and peptide complex that exfoliates to support the skin's renewal process," she says. That means it’ll go to work on discoloration and fine lines on your face and body while you sleep, since it’s a night treatment.

She highlights the intensive humectant and emollient moisturizers and vitamins that keep the skin hydrated for 24 hours as essential for skin firming and smoothing. You can see that in the texture; it’s rich and thick but still rubs in easily and dries quickly, so it’s not a pain to put on before bed.

A great place to give it a go first might be the neck and chest, where wrinkles tend to start popping up sooner than we all might like. Just keep in mind your skin type. Women with oily or combination skin might find it a tad heavy, so start with a pea-sized amount on the face and only add more as needed. Those with normal or dry skin will love this one due to its wonderfully hydrating formula.

Although Revision is a pricey pick, Dr. Nazarian argues it’s well worth the splurge because of the science-backed results and clinical trials. “It combines a cocktail of peptides and antioxidants to promote collagen, prevent breakdown, and ingredients like glucosamine to support cell turnover.” In other words, this product will help tighten loose skin.

BodiContour can be used before and after professional treatments to help enhance your results. However, you should wait until any broken skin is fully healed after your procedure before incorporating this cream back into your routine.

Dr. Sartor likes the hyaluronic acid in the formula as well but notes that the lotion is part of a three-step regimen. She thinks the brand’s promised results—from the fading of sun damage to the tightening of dimply, saggy skin—will be seen with use of the entire system. And even if a little lotion does go a long way, the instructions do recommend applying it twice a day and exfoliating twice a week. So with that does come a significant investment of time and money.

It's not called Magic Cream for nothing. This silky body cream blends caffeine and hydrating all-star hyaluronic acid to smooth and firm the skin. "It also includes the iconic magic 8 matrix, which includes vitamin C and E, aloe vera, camellia oil, rosehip oil, and shea butter, plus moisturizing frangipani flower extract," says dermatologist Dr. Marisa Garshick, MD. "Together this helps to brighten the skin and leave the skin glowing."

Of all the formulas Blundell tried, the Magic Body Cream is the one that left the most noticeable sheen and slight blurring effect on her skin. Putting it on feels luxurious, too; it’s rich but not so heavy that it doesn’t blend well, and it has a similar fragrance to its sister product, Magic Cream anti-aging face moisturizer. The only downside? At $65 a pop, it’s expensive, so Blundell saves it for nights when she’s showing a little skin or wants to target visible areas like the arms, legs, and tummy when sporting resort wear.

StriVectin is well regarded as a top-tier line for anti-aging and skin-firming products, and this rich body cream is a shining example of why the brand has a cult-like following among beauty insiders. And it all starts with the ingredients. A combination of turmeric root and jojoba seed extracts paired with a buttery blend of shea, murumuru, and cupuacu provide deep moisture to improve the look of skin texture and crepiness, says dermatologist Brendan Camp, MD. The turmeric helps brighten uneven skin tone while peptides and jojoba seed extract work together to tighten the skin and make it appear visibly more firm.

If you’re looking to fight back against particularly crepey arms or kneecaps, Dr. Sartor points out that this formula does include more antioxidants than some of the less expensive drugstore options. She also highlights the caffeine and collagen peptides, which work in tandem with the other firming extracts mentioned above. “This would be a good option for more mature skin in need of a richer moisturizer with more skin benefits,” she says.Although spending $44 might seem like a lot, there are other luxury anti-aging lotions out there selling for $165 to $220. If it helps, each container will last around 6 to 12 weeks, depending on how often you apply and if you’re slathering all over or just targeting a smaller area of your body. Regardless, even if you buy a few replacements in the year at $176, you get a year’s worth of product for significantly less than if you were splurging on a single high-end firming body lotion.

If you’re looking for an ultralight, gel-like product that can smooth, plump, and deliver silky-to-the-touch skin, then Nécessaire The Body Serum is the best pick for you. The formula is made with gentle clean ingredients that don’t skimp on quality. It combines ceramides with five molecular weights of hyaluronic acid which provides multilevel hydration. The result: a plumping finish that delivers a bit of lift and tautness. Glycerin further moisturizes the skin, while aloe vera calms redness and irritation. There’s also niacinamide for fine line-fighting benefits.

I’ve been using this serum on and off for a few years, and I can confidently attest to its effectiveness. It helps clear up eczema flare-ups, and has been a beauty lifesaver during the winter when it’s freezing outdoors and my radiator is cranked up inside. A single layer of the clear serum soaks into my skin in seconds, and if your skin is extra parched like mine is then you can apply additional layers as needed without pilling or leaving behind a sticky mess. It’s a year-round must-have for me because in the spring and summer I can just get away with using this instead of a thick lotion or cream.

“This serum does not have any firming ingredients but instead contains hyaluronic acid to plump skin appearance and ceramides to repair the skin barrier,” says Dr. Sartor. “This serum also contains lecithin to help prevent further water loss from the skin surface.”

Honestly, the only downside with this serum is that it’s fragrance-free. Nécessaire does fragrances so incredibly well that I wish they extended their enticing aromas into The Body Serum as well. Still, I fully stand by this serum and if you’re on the fence give it a go and see for yourself. With Amazon Prime’s signature two-day shipping and a 30-day money-back guarantee you have extra reassurance to treat yourself.

You’ve probably been using body lotion since middle school, and firming formulas look and feel roughly the same. They’re applied the same way, too; just massage a dollop into the skin, let it dry for a bit, and you’re good to go on with your day. A few key features, though, are what can separate a good option from a great one, and this is what you’ll want to consider when shopping for the best firming body lotions.

For dermatologist Dr. Rachel Nazarian, MD, certain ingredients are a must if you’re looking to tone and improve the skin’s texture.

Ultimately, whatever lotion, oil, serum, or cream you choose comes down to your skin’s needs. On the most basic level, sometimes it’s just a matter of texture preference—maybe you like the lightness of an oil or serum and want to go that route, or the richness of a cream is what you gravitate toward in the colder months. But some skin types really do fare better with certain formats over others, so you’ll want to keep that in mind.

Serums, gels, and lotions are lightweight and generally better suited for women under 40 with normal or acne-prone skin. Because they’re not heavy, they’re also fantastic if you have sensitive skin all over. You can follow it up with a cream as spot treatment in areas like your kneecaps and elbows that require more moisturization, says Dr. Sartor.

Creams are thick and deeply hydrating, making them helpful for dry and mature skin. You can also use them if you have sensitive skin. However, there is a trade-off. Hyaluronic acid penetrates the skin more easily in lighter serums and gels, so you might need to choose between a gentler product and a more effective moisturizer.

Though not as important as ingredients or format, size can matter when it comes to choosing a firming body lotion, mainly because it can factor into a product’s price and usage. If you want to make a smaller, more expensive lotion go further, consider applying it to target areas—think the butt, thighs, tummy, or upper arms. Consistency is key, though, so a product that you can use more frequently could be better than something you’d have to use sparingly.

Dr. Nava Greenfield, MD, is a board-certified dermatologist at Schweiger Dermatology Group in New York City.

Dr. Rachel Nazarian MD, FAAD, is a board-certified dermatologist with Schweiger Dermatology Group in New York City.

Dr. Quynh-Giao Sartor, MD, FAAD, is a board-certified dermatologist at Westlake Dermatology in Houston, Texas.

Dr. Lauren Penzi, MD, is a board-certified dermatologist at MDCS Dermatology: Medical Dermatology & Cosmetic Surgery in New York.

Dr. Marisa Garshick, MD, FAAD, is a board-certified dermatologist and assistant clinical professor of dermatology at Cornell - New York Presbyterian Medical Center.

Dr. Brendan Camp, MD, FAAD, is a board-certified dermatologist at MDCS Dermatology in New York.

It’s important to manage your expectations for firming lotions—they’re not the cure-all for sagging skin. Severe laxity and deep folds aren’t going to disappear overnight, but your skin will perk up and even plump a bit temporarily upon application.

“You can expect to see your skin slowly showing fewer fine lines and less sag,” says Dr. Greenfield. “A firming cream also has the potential to introduce nutrients that allow your skin to feel smoother and more supple.”

Proper timing is key for absorption and even application, so do yourself a favor and apply right after you’ve just bathed so it sinks in easily, especially if you’re only using this kind of product once a day.

“It is best to apply body lotion when your skin is still damp from a shower but not wet,” says Dr. Greenfield. “Towel dried is optimal. After exfoliating, it is crucial to apply a moisturizer. Best results will ultimately be with consistent and liberal use.”

“Creams are not capable of the same type of tightening that lasers and surgical options can offer,” says Dr. Nazarian. “Despite this, with consistent, continued use, you can certainly see improvement in laxity over time.” But again, commitment to regular use will impact results because everyone’s skin is fighting an uphill battle to a certain extent, at least when it comes to the loss of skin firmness and volume. For the best results, you have to commit to using one regularly to improve the quality of skin laxity, says Dr. Nazarian.

The short answer is yes—but with the caveat that it’s possible to have some kind of a reaction to any body lotion or cream. “Most of these body firming lotions have very little risk,” says Dr. Nazarian. “They are often directed to be used daily, some even twice a day. Major risks include irritation from one of the ingredients or a potential allergy to one of the ingredients.”

Just steer clear of anything with retinol in it, if you’re nursing or pregnant, and discontinue use of a product you have a negative reaction to. “Occasionally, people may experience drying of their skin, especially if the ingredients have the ability to decrease oil production, such as with retinol,” says Dr. Nazarian. “Monitor for those changes and decrease use if they are noted.”

Cranking up my personal space heater creates a warm, dry environment that dehydrates my skin and lips, leaving them dry, flaky, and sometimes painful. While drinking water and not licking lips can help, dermatologists say those aren’t the only reasons they get chapped.

Our lips have a unique anatomy. They have thinner skin, low water retention, and fewer oil glands than the rest of our face. That makes them more prone to dryness, says dermatologist Teresa Song, MD.

A good lip balm hydrates, seals in moisture, prevents cracking, and protects the skin barrier from harsh elements, she says. That’s where the ingredients shine and separate good lip balms from great ones. Once you order one of these editor-tested, dermatologist-recommended lip balms, reapplication is key. Dr. Song advises reapplying every two to six hours, and once before bed.

The bottom line: You need something that's going to keep your pout hydrated and supple all year long. Thankfully, we tapped four dermatologists to get their input on what to look for in the best lip balms and which ones they recommend to their clientele. Then, we took matters into our own hands and tested them all ourselves, narrowing down our list to the 11 best lip balms for a wide range of different concerns. Before diving into our list, keep reading to discover what to look for when shopping for your new balm.

Need more proof that Laneige locks in moisture overnight? Colbert fell asleep with it on and woke up facing the fan with lips still soft and moisturized. “It’s perfect after exfoliating and lasts through a night of tossing and turning,” she says.

Laneige is also one of the rare lip masks that includes a tiny spatula for mess-free application. The spatula elevates my selfcare routine and ensures that I scoop the last drop of product before I reorder a replacement.

I personally love all the fun flavors it comes in (there are eight options on Amazon), but if fragrances aren't your thing, you might not love this product as much as I do.

For our annual Skincare Awards package, WH's beauty team tested hundreds of new beauty products. Mogg crowned this new drop her ultimate lip balm because it delivers intense moisture, comes in sheer colors, and has fun packaging.

A blend of zinc, copper, and magnesium hydrates her dry lips and banana juice retains moisture even after she rubs excess product off. It's also infused with coconut and aloe extracts to condition and smooth chapped lips, which earned it a permanent spot in Mogg's daily beauty routine.

Her favorite part about this balm is by far the deliciously sweet scent and fruity flavors. Mogg found the aromas so enticing that she was tempted to eat them. Milk Makeup is available in seven colors, including Quench, a brown beige with a coconut flavor, and Werk Out, a dusty rose that tastes like watermelon.

Associate fitness editor Olivia Luppino is also a fan because it applies smoothly and nourishes her lips. She says it’s also only slightly sticky compared to the other lip balms she tested, such as Aquaphor and Rhode.

Though we fully stand behind this pick, the fruity smell lingers—you should skip it if you don't enjoy sweet scents.

Both Hailey Bieber and her skincare brand, Rhode, have become synonymous with "glazed donut skin," and this moisturizing lip treatment gives my lips that same effect. Most lip glosses leave behind a sticky feel or oily finish, but not Rhode. It provides a super-hydrating feel, with a glossy finish and non-sticky feel. No wonder we crowned it the best lip treatment in our 2023 Beauty Awards. “This one mixes the usual moisturizing suspects like shea butter and natural oils with peptides to plump,” says Underwood.

And we’re not the only fans. Dermatologist Azadeh Shirazi, MD, highlights the combination of nourishing shea butter and collagen-supporting, lip-plumping peptides as standout ingredients. It’s also made with vitamin E, which retains moisture and provides antioxidant protection. Dr. Shirazi likes the rich texture, which helps hydrate and protect dry lips.While the option linked here is the unscented version, you can buy the balm in four additional flavors: strawberry, salted caramel, vanilla, and watermelon. FWIW, Luppino is a big fan of the unscented, untinted version because she prefers a natural look with a glossy finish.I adore Rhode, but Luppino says it’s the thickest and stickiest lip balm, so she doesn’t use it daily. That said, it’s still a nourishing balm with a glossy finish—and it plays nicely with makeup or when layered on its own. And FWIW, I found the tinted versions aren’t grainy. Espresso layered over a pinky-nude lipstick, like my holy grail Charlotte Tilbury Pillow Talk Original, is a stunning combination.

If the word "plumper" scares you, don't worry—BeautyStat doesn't contain menthol, so it won't cause that uncomfortable tingly feeling. Instead, it relies on two peptides to hydrate and plump fine lines for a fuller pout. The volumized look—elimination of lip lines and feathering—lasted up to two hours, and the hydration lingered longer. Most importantly, the results are subtle without painful injections, which is always a win. It just makes your lips look super shiny and, if we do say so ourselves, kissable.

BeautyStat also blends sodium hyaluronate and squalane for extra hydration without feeling heavy or goopy on my lips. Its lightweight texture coats my lips in four colors—ranging from Natural Peach and Baby Pink to my personal favorite Butter Beige, a neutral-pink with a light coat of color. There’s also Mocha, a rich brown that looks gorgeous on both melanin-rich and fair complexions.

It’s also packed with zinc oxide, a mineral SPF that doesn’t leave behind an ashy tint on my lips. It’s also gentle compared to chemical active ingredients, like avobenzone. Not to mention it’s enriched with vitamin C to help repair environmental damage and brighten an uneven skin tone.

Best of all? There’s no off-putting fragrance. Just a light, vanilla-creamsicle scent that adds a welcome touch of summer despite the chilly weather.

If you want to go the natural route, I have just the pick for you: Evolvetogether's plant-powered lip balm, which taps coconut oil, shea butter, and jojoba seed oil to coat the lips in a smooth, buttery veil. The best part? There's zero thick or sticky residue left behind. Just the satiny feeling of the natural butters, lavender and chamomile oils. Dr. Song notes the simple and clean formula is effective for light moisture, making it a great fit for anyone who hates the goopy feeling of thicker lip masks or lives somewhere warm year-round.

When Dr. Song says light moisture, she really means it. Colbert likes it for daily wear, but needed to reapply frequently after riding on the back of her friend’s motorcycle for 20 minutes. “When I apply it after my skincare routine I can sit through a few hours of TV and doomscrolling and still have my lips feeling moisturized,” she says.

I love that this balm is available in two different scents—Provence and Anguilla—to suit your mood. I’ve only tried Provence, which is a mix of chamomile, lavender, and vanilla. It smells gorgeous and fresh—never overpowering.Something to note: This formula contains beeswax, so it's not a great option for the vegans out there.

Laneige remains my favorite lip mask, but this one from Ilia is fragrance-free, and only has a light lavender scent from its ingredients, which is great if you have a sensitive nose or skin. I keep this formula in my work tote because I'm not always in the mood for an aroma, but it also never slacks on deep hydration. After applying it nightly for a month, my lips always felt super moisturized and never chapped, which is a huge plus.

“There's nothing worse to me than an artificial fruit taste accidentally getting in my mouth,” says Ritchey. She’s a big fan of this fragrance-free balm and highlights its non-sticky, super moisturizing formula that left her lips feeling brand new after application.

What else makes it a noteworthy inclusion? Ilia combines salicornia, which is a type of flowering plant, with hyaluronic acid to boost hydration and support the skin barrier, says dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD. It also contains papaya enzymes, which help to get rid of dead skin cells. Due to the fruit's exfoliating properties, you should only use this twice daily to avoid overscrubbing your lips.

The only downside with this lip mask is that it comes in a pot instead of a squeezable tube, so it’s not as clean when applying. For Ritchey and her longer nails that’s a minor problem. “It's difficult to get the product out of the container, especially when it's towards the bottom,” she says. “However, the product is good enough that it's worth living with the difficult container!” If you’re also sporting longer nails, this balm easily applies with a cotton bud. And since it’s clear, don’t be surprised if your partner tries to swipe this one from your medicine cabinet. Yup, it’s that good.

This Women's Health Skincare Award-winning balm features a piña colada–esque flavor that brings a tropical touch to Underwood’s mornings. But most importantly, it’s an untinted SPF lip balm that doesn’t have the unpleasant sunscreen taste. We like to wear it on its own each morning for the most natural appearance.

We're also impressed by the epic lineup of nourishing ingredients, like lanolin. Research shows that lanolin can reduce transepidermal water loss (TEWL) by up to 30%, ensuring our lips are amply moisturized. However, lanolin can irritate some people, according to the American Academy of Dermatology. While that hasn’t been Underwood’s experience, if that happens to you, it’s best to stop using this one.

Still, the thicker formula is also infused with a plethora of castor seed oil, beeswax, shea butter, grapeseed oil, vitamin E, and coconut oil. This broad-spectrum sunscreen combines four types of active chemical ingredients that provide SPF 30 coverage that avoids a white cast.

Another limitation to this balm? We need a separate lip balm for nighttime—wearing SPF to bed doesn't make sense since we’re not exposed to harmful ultraviolet rays while we slumber.

Dr. Song name-checked three types of ingredients to watch for—humectants, emollients, and occlusives—and shared how they keep the lips hydrated, smooth, and protected.

You’ll want to stay away from alcohol, which causes excessive dryness. Mineral oil may clog pores around the lips, and strong fragrances can lead to irritation and rashes. Though menthol, camphor, and phenol have a cooling sensation, they will irritate and dry the lips over time.

Dr. Song also recommends swapping out lip balms when seasons change and when you're traveling to a different climate. Use lighter formulas such as Rhode’s Peptide Lip Treatment in warm or humid climates and thicker formulas like the Laneige Lip Mask in cold or dry weather.

To find the best lip balms, I reevaluated my massive collection of products. I considered their ingredients and consistency, as well as their functional and cosmetic benefits. For example, I evaluated how long the hydration lasted and how sticky each swipe felt.

While my favorites range from $5 to $30, I didn’t notice a decline in the quality or feel of more affordable lip balms, nor did pricier picks equate to dramatic hydration.

Additionally, I ensured there was a mix of lightweight formulas for daily wear and heavier balms for overnight use. Because I love experimenting with my lipstick and lip liner combos, I awarded bonus points to balms that come in a variety of tints. I also factored in how vibrant or sheer each hue was on its own and how they layered with makeup. There are clear options for anyone who prefers a more natural look.

To further refine the list, I asked four dermatologists about their go-to picks. I also recruited other WH staffers: beauty director Brian Underwood, beauty editorial assistant Katie Mogg, and associate health and wellness editor Addison Aloian. Beauty contributors Lily Wohlner and Danielle Jackson joined as testers for this story.

When we initially published this story in February 2024, we featured 20 lip balms. For our latest 2026 update, we tried 40 lip balms over a year and settled on 10 tried-and-true recommendations that we’re actually using this fall and beyond. They're all aligned with dermatological guidance and nourish our lips for hours.

It seemed illogical to pay $30 a month for software that just offered a basic sales page, especially without any integrated email service provider.

As I spent more time with Stan Store, my perspective began to shift. I realized that for someone completely new to online marketing, who might be overwhelmed by the complexities of building and creating a landing or sales page, Stan Store could actually make a lot of sense.

It’s tailored for beginners, offering them a straightforward entry point into the world of digital marketing.

So, who’s going to love Stan Store? Pretty much anyone aiming to make a buck online through digital products or services. If you’re like me, trying to turn those ‘link in bio’ clicks into actual sales, then Stan Store is your go-to.

Let me break it down for you. Stan Store is a hit with a wide range of creators and businesses, but from my experience, it’s a total game-changer for:

And hey, even if you’re in the business of selling physical goods, Stan Store can be a killer tool for growing your email list or hosting online events.

Just a heads up though – selling physical products directly through Stan Store isn’t on the table just yet.

Picture this: I’m on TikTok or Instagram Stories, chatting about my latest digital product – let’s say it’s an eBook or a PDF.

In the past, I’d direct my followers to the ‘link in my bio’, which would then send them off to another site, like my website. There, they’d have to play detective to find the product I was talking about, or sit through endless page loads.

But with Stan Store, things get a whole lot smoother. The ‘link in my bio’ is now the store itself. Followers can hit that link, buy what they want right there and then, without being shunted off to a different site.

The best part? They can hop right back to Instagram or TikTok without feeling like they ever left. It’s all about keeping it simple and seamless – and that’s what Stan Store nails perfectly.

The convenience and accessibility of Stan Store are what eventually changed my initial skepticism. The platform allows anyone, regardless of their technical skill, to quickly set up a landing or sales page.

In conclusion, while Stan Store might not be the one-size-fits-all solution for every online entrepreneur, it certainly has carved out its niche. It’s a platform that understands and caters to the needs of digital content creators, making it a worthwhile consideration for those in its target demographic.

As with any tool, it’s about finding the right fit for your specific needs, and for many creators, Stan Store could be just that.

Systeme.io has burst onto the digital marketing scene, brandishing a bold claim as an all-in-one, free platform.

Let’s face it, when you hear something like that, your first thought is, “This has got to be too good to be true.”

That was my initial reaction too. A free, do-it-all software that doesn’t suck? Highly doubtful.

But here’s the shocker: Systeme.io isn’t just blowing smoke. It’s a game-changer. As someone who’s navigated the maze of digital marketing tools, I was prepared for disappointment. Yet, Systeme.io left me floored with its capabilities.

Take it from someone who’s been around the block with the likes of ConvertKit, AWeber, and MailChimp. These giants lure you in with free offerings, only to tighten the screws when your audience grows. Then there’s WordPress.org – great for setting up a blog, but it’s like climbing Everest if you’re a newbie.

Systeme.io, on the other hand, is a beast of a different nature. Offering highly effective landing pages and robust sales funnels with professional templates for free? That’s unheard of. It’s like stumbling upon a treasure chest in your backyard.

My first foray into landing page software was with ClickFunnels, an undeniably powerful tool. But once the 14-day trial evaporates, you’re staring down the barrel of a $100 monthly fee. Worth it if you’re a pro, but a gut punch for beginners.

Yes, you can test it out 100% completely FREE.

And when the time comes to open your wallet, it’s less than $30 a month – an absolute steal for the arsenal of tools you’re getting.

Absolutely. It’s a diamond in the rough, especially for those just starting their digital marketing journey. For the veterans, it might not have the same allure, but for the rookies, it’s a godsend. Forget the skepticism; Systeme.io is a disruptor that’s here to stay.

The platform serves a multifaceted purpose, aiming to simplify the digital marketing process. It’s designed for entrepreneurs and businesses seeking an integrated solution for email marketing, sales funnels, website building, and more.

The importance of such a tool lies in its ability to streamline various marketing tasks, which are often scattered across different platforms, into one cohesive system.

The user interface of Systeme.io? It’s okay, but let’s not sugarcoat it. For a newbie who’s never dabbled in sales funnels or email campaigns, it can feel like being thrown into the deep end. It’s not the sleek, intuitive experience that tech gurus might rave about. But, and this is a big but, Systeme.io doesn’t just leave you hanging.

The saving grace here is their tutorials. These are goldmines for beginners. They walk you through the process, breaking down what could be an overwhelming experience into manageable chunks. So, while the interface might not win any beauty contests, the support system in place is BIG help.

At the core of Systeme.io are several key features that make it a comprehensive digital marketing solution. These include email marketing capabilities, sales funnel creation tools, a website builder, options for hosting membership sites, and affiliate program management.

Each of these features is designed to work seamlessly with the others, providing a unified experience. For instance, the email marketing service is notably efficient, rivaling established providers like ConvertKit, AWeber, and MailChimp, especially with its free subscription model that remains functional up to a certain point.

Here’s a sample template they offer for their email campaigns:

Here’s a breakdown of all the features Systeme.io offers:

And if here’s a fancy table to help simplify it even more:

When we talk about the cost-effectiveness of Systeme.io, we’re looking at a platform that offers a substantial suite of features without the hefty price tag that usually accompanies such versatility.

For starters, Systeme.io’s freemium model is a standout in the digital marketing space (click here to open a free account today). You can manage up to 2,000 contacts and create three sales funnels without spending a penny. This is a significant advantage for entrepreneurs and small businesses where every dollar counts.

To put this into perspective, let’s compare it with some industry counterparts. Platforms like ClickFunnels and Kartra, while offering robust functionalities, start their pricing at around $97 to $99 per month after their trial periods. This can be a steep investment for those just starting out.

In contrast, Systeme.io not only allows you to test the waters for free but also keeps the costs low even when you upgrade. Their paid plans, offering a broader range of features, start at less than $30 a month.

This pricing strategy makes advanced digital marketing tools accessible to a wider audience, breaking down the financial barriers that often hinder small businesses and startups.

The all-in-one nature of Systeme.io is its hallmark. It consolidates various marketing tools into one cohesive platform. This integration means you can manage email campaigns, build sales funnels, create websites, and even run affiliate programs without having to switch between different software. For many users, this integration simplifies the digital marketing process significantly, allowing for a more streamlined workflow.

However, it’s important to recognize that while Systeme.io covers a broad spectrum of functionalities, it may not offer the same depth as specialized standalone tools in each specific area.

For instance, while its email marketing capabilities are robust, they might not have the advanced features of a dedicated email marketing service.

Similarly, its website builder is competent for basic to intermediate needs, but it might not satisfy users looking for highly advanced web design features.

Systeme.io aims to be user-friendly, and for the most part, it achieves this goal. The interface is designed to be intuitive, especially for those who have basic familiarity with digital marketing tools. However, for complete beginners, there can be a learning curve.

The platform offers a range of tutorials and support materials, which are invaluable for new users. I’ve watched (and rewatched) several of these tutorials to lean how to use their software.

These resources are designed to help users navigate through the initial complexity and make the most out of the platform’s features.

Let’s get real about customization in Systeme.io. It’s got a decent selection of templates and the interface won’t make you pull your hair out, but if you’re looking to really dive deep into customization, you might hit a wall.

For those who have grand visions of a highly unique and tailored digital presence, Systeme.io can feel a bit like playing with kid gloves. It’s great for getting you up and running, but for the more ambitious or specific design needs, it’s not quite the creative playground you might be looking for.

Now, onto scalability. Systeme.io is like that compact car that’s perfect for city driving but struggles a bit on the open highway. For small businesses or solo entrepreneurs just starting out, it’s a match made in heaven. But as your business grows and your needs become more complex, Systeme.io might start to feel a bit cramped.

This is especially true for larger businesses or those niche ventures that need more than just the basics. As you scale up, you might find yourself needing more sophisticated tools and features that Systeme.io doesn’t offer.

Plus, when it comes to playing nice with other tools or services you might be using, Systeme.io isn’t always the most cooperative. It works well within its own confines but doesn’t always reach out to others easily.

Here’s a quick rundown on the pros and cons of Systeme.io

When compared to competitors, Systeme.io’s pricing is highly competitive. For instance, platforms like ClickFunnels offer powerful functionality but at a higher cost, typically starting at around $100 per month after a free trial. This can be a significant investment, especially for new entrepreneurs or small businesses.

In contrast, Systeme.io’s paid plans, which provide access to a broader range of features, are more affordable, starting at less than $30 a month.

To provide a broader perspective, let’s compare Systeme.io with other popular tools in the market:

This comparison shows that while Systeme.io offers a comprehensive suite of tools at an affordable price, platforms like HubSpot and Kartra provide more advanced features in certain areas but at a higher cost. ClickFunnels, on the other hand, is more expensive but offers highly customizable funnel-building capabilities.

User reviews and testimonials play a crucial role in understanding the real-world effectiveness of Systeme.io. Many users have shared success stories, highlighting how the platform has helped them streamline their marketing efforts and grow their businesses.

Anatomy Of A Fall Ending Explained: Was Daniel Lying?

📅 2024-01-08  |  Read Source →

At the end of Anatomy of a Fall, Sandra is acquitted, although the facts of the case still aren't entirely clear, making the true cause of Samuel's death ambiguous. The 2023 movie is a legal drama from French director Justine Triet, featuring performances from Sandra Hüller, Swann Arlaud, Samuel Theis, Milo Machado Graner, and more. Anatomy of a Fall received great reviews and enjoyed lots of awards success, winning the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival and picking up five Oscars 2024 nominations, winning for Best Original Screenplay.

After the mysterious death of her husband, Samuel (Samuel Theis), Sandra Voyter (Sandra Hüller) becomes the prime suspect. Sandra's best defense is to claim Samuel died by suicide, which even she tells her lawyer, Vincent (Swann Arlaud), is implausible at first. The only person who can back up her version of events is her blind son, Daniel (Milo Machado Graner). When an audio recording revealed in court proves she was also covering up evidence of domestic turmoil, Daniel appears to have doubts about her innocence but ultimately gives testimony that leads to her acquittal.

Initially, Daniel said he heard Sandra and Samuel having a casual conversation as he went past the shed to walk the dog, Snoop. He was positive he was standing next to the shed because of the texture of the tape Samuel put there for him to identify the location.

It's entirely possible recreating the moment jogged Daniel's memory, but it's also conspicuous that he changed his story to maintain a favorable outlook for Sandra at the end of Anatomy of a Fall.

When the investigators tried to recreate the scenario to determine how loud Sandra and Samuel had to be talking to match his story, Samuel suddenly changed his testimony to say he was inside the front door. It's entirely possible recreating the moment jogged Daniel's memory, but it's also conspicuous that he changed his story to maintain a favorable outlook for Sandra at the end of Anatomy of a Fall.

Daniel says his memories returned to him again at the last second, providing a new testimony about Snoop eating aspirin from Samuel's vomit to back up Sandra's claim of an alleged suicide attempt. Once again, Daniel's testimony is conveniently altered to favor Sandra's version of events, which supports a suicide theory Sandra didn't even initially agree with when strategizing with Vincent. Daniel's story is plausible, but his odd behavior, asking Sandra to leave the house, and having Snoop eat aspirin before changing his story invites skepticism, especially considering his story seemed to be the deciding factor.

The audio recording Samuel makes of his fight with Sandra is one of the most damning pieces of evidence against her, especially since she tried to cover up the fact that they fought at all, but its very existence calls other factors into question. As Sandra says, it's possible Samuel provoked the fight to get a recording. If true, the recording may have been intended for use as literary inspiration, but if he'd already begun contemplating suicide (as his alleged previous suicide attempt would indicate), then the recording may have been an attempt to implicate Sandra in his death.

If he was legitimately jealous and resentful of Sandra's success, particularly after she used one of his novel ideas in her own writing, the claims made in the recording tarnish her professionally, in addition to the hit her reputation would take from being indicted in the first place.

Considering he was aware of the recording and Sandra wasn't, his accusations against her, while containing legitimate frustrations, could also be performative, knowing the recording would be discovered and played in court after his death. If he was legitimately jealous and resentful of Sandra's success, particularly after she used one of his novel ideas in her own writing, the claims made in the recording tarnish her professionally, in addition to the hit her reputation would take from being indicted in the first place.

Granted, Sandra tells Vincent his depiction of Samuel's "final year" wasn't an accurate reflection, so she may not agree with that theory, although the existence of the recording makes it plausible.

The only flashbacks in the movie, Samuel's argument with Sandra and his conversation in the car with Daniel, are presented as possible versions of the story, through the audio recording and Daniel's recollection, rather than moments to be taken as fact.

After Sandra is acquitted, she goes to dinner with Vincent and says she feels weird because there's normally a reward for winning. While avoiding a conviction is certainly a form of reward for her, if she's innocent, then she's now left to process Samuel's suicide for the first time. Sandra initially disagreed with the idea that Samuel died by suicide and even disagreed with Vincent's depiction of "Samuel's final year" as presented in court.

She may never truly escape her guilt as Daniel will be a constant reminder.

For that to be the theory that exonerates her leaves Sandra to process complicated emotions associated with her husband's death for the first time or may even leave her wondering about some other cause. There is also the lingering awkwardness with Daniel. Despite the fact that his testimony saved her, they are both now aware that he at least considered for a time that his mother killed his father.

On the other hand, if Sandra truly did kill Samuel, she now has to live a lie for the rest of her life, including lying to Daniel. Additionally, if she was lying about Samuel's suicide to cover up her involvement, Daniel may have also been lying to back her up, in which case she knows Daniel is aware of her deception.

Unfortunately, there's no clear explanation for what truly happened to Samuel, and while Sandra may have certainty of her guilt or innocence, it may not be possible for anyone else, including Daniel, to ever truly trust her version of events. For example, the blood splatter and autopsy indicate he was likely struck with a weapon before he fell, but at the same time, it's improbable that Sandra was able to lift and push him over the edge in the way the prosecutor indicated. No single theory fully accounts for both the blood splatter and the body falling where it did.

The coroner determines that Samuel received a blow to the head before hitting the ground, but the autopsy proves inconclusive and offers no hard evidence. The prosecution brings in a blood spatter expert who testifies that Samuel's death must have come from an intentional blow to the head, delivered by another human, before his fall. He's clearly convinced of his interpretation and has video simulations to help prove it. A second expert says Samuel fell onto a shed, then bounced into the air, his body spinning, releasing blood in exactly the pattern discovered.

Looking closely at the shed after Samuel falls in the beginning of the movie, there appears to be a point of impact where his head could have hit, aligning with the defense's blood splatter theory, but it's still not enough to provide any decisive conclusion about the true nature of Samuel's death.

Daniel's testimony is equally shaky, especially considering his own conflict of interest. He knows his testimony could be the strongest factor in influencing his mother's verdict, but he doesn't know if he can fully trust his mom, which is why he seeks advice from Marge (Jehnny Beth), who unfortunately can't comment on the case to him.

Memory is fallible, so his multiple shifting testimonies are easy to explain, but the fact that his testimony always shifts in favor of Sandra and only in response to evidence that looks bad for her, makes it look like he's changing his story to protect her.

In his final testimony, Daniel recalls that while he and Samuel were driving Snoop to the veterinarian, his father spoke to him about the need to be prepared that those he loves will die. Samuel was specifically talking about Snoop's short lifespan, but Daniel concludes that it reflected his father's own suicidal thoughts. On the witness stand, he says that if his mother did this, he can't understand it, but if his father did it, he can. Knowing he can't be certain what happened, he admits it's easier to believe Samuel died by suicide than that Sandra was a murderer. Daniel's testimony works, and Sandra is acquitted.

As the audience, we know even more than the investigators and prosecution, making Sandra's position even more complicated. On one hand, she doubted the suicide theory from the start, but if she were guilty she should be more eager to support the strongest alibi. Looking closely at the shed after Samuel falls in the beginning of the movie, there appears to be a point of impact where his head could have hit, aligning with the defense's blood splatter theory, but it's still not enough to provide any decisive conclusion about the true nature of Samuel's death.

At the end of Anatomy of a Fall, there's still a lot of ambiguity around how Samuel died and how truthful Sandra and Daniel are. As Sandra tells Samuel's therapist:

"What you say is just a part of the whole situation. You know. I mean, sometimes a couple is kind of a chaos and everybody is lost."

Anatomy of a Fall ends not with Sandra alongside her son, but with their dog, Snoop. It's a moment that, aside from showcasing the unconditional love of a dog, highlights how alone Sandra still is. Her husband is dead, and while her son may or may not have lied to protect her, there's still a great distance between them. Having Snoop in there is an important reminder to Sandra there is still love for her, while simultaneously reflecting on her loss and grief.

Snoop was played by a border collie named Messi.

Justine Triet doesn't want to over-explain Anatomy of a Fall's ending, which is why the writer-director purposefully made things ambiguous. However, just like audiences, she has her own ideas and feelings about what the truth might actually be. In an interview with The Wrap, she explained that finding the "doubt" was the key to the ending, but when asked how she responds to questions of whether Sandra was guilty or not, she said:

Well, what can I say? It’s the same thing as in life. Who knows the real truth? To me, I think maybe that Sandra could be not guilty of murder but responsible for pushing him to commit suicide. Maybe? It’s a question of: What are we all responsible for in our lives? The film is opening so many other doors. And in a way, I think, well, she lied two times in the movie. So maybe we can cast doubt on her and say, “Hmm, is it possible she did do it?” But I don’t want to say that.

Sandra Hüller has described her own version of that uncertainty. She said that two days before filming started, she called Triet and thought, "What if she actually tricks me into something?" She had two days to decide what to do, and she realized it's really not so important whether Sandra is a murderer or not. As Hüller put it, it's really about what other people think of her.

While the Anatomy of a Fall ending leaves plenty of possibilities of Sandra being guilty, the real purpose behind the movie is the exploration of this marriage. Part of Sandra's frustration is having to defend aspects of her marriage from people who could not possibly know the truth as she does. From the prosecutors to Samuel's therapist to the spectators getting a glimpse inside her intimate world, they are deciding what her marriage was based on very little information.

Looking at the ending of the movie as if Sandra is innocent provides perhaps the most compelling arc. While her marriage to Samuel was not perfect, there were no issues that would drive her to murder him. Yet Anatomy of a Fall's courtroom scenes pick apart every aspect of their relationship, magnifying hard moments and blowing them out of proportion.

It's frustrating for Sandra that it's almost impossible to combat the assumptions that are made based on this "evidence". She cannot convince people that there is a difference between an argument between a couple and a conflict that leads to death. In that sense, Daniel is the only one who can save her. With no one else able to see what she sees, Daniel chooses to believe his mother in the Anatomy of a Fall ending, even if he might lie in his testimony. His testimony gives the court a believable suicide version of Samuel's death, but it doesn't prove what happened. Daniel chooses the version of his father's death that he can survive, and the movie never confirms that he invented his final testimony.

Anatomy of a Fall arrived to more-or-less universal praise when it premiered in 2023. Director Justin Triet's legal drama currently holds a 96% critical score and 90% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. These high numbers represent both the quality of Anatomy of a Fall overall, and the strength of its ending, since movies based on complex legal mysteries are rarely (if ever) well received if the story is betrayed by a sub-par ending. The main praise for Anatomy of a Fall was in two areas - the performance of Sandra Hüller, and the emotional impact of the story. As far as the latter is concerned, the ending is incredibly important.

For many critics and audiences alike, the key strength of the ending of Anatomy of a Fall was the way it decompresses the immense tension building throughout the rest of the film, while also leaving things on an ambiguous note. It was incredibly risky for Justin Triet to end the story without fully clarifying if Sandra was guilty or not, but walking this narrative tightrope ultimately became the key strength of the final moments.

By refusing to elaborate on Sandra's guilt or innocence, the Anatomy of a Fall ending helped ensure the movie was an intimate psychological character study. Had a definitive answer been given, it would have shifted the tone entirely, especially during second or third viewings. By keeping the possibility that Sandra could be a victim of a terrible situation or the perpetrator of a murder, none of the thematic character-driven depth of Anatomy of a Fall is lost during the final moments.

Ultimately, the ending of Anatomy of a Fall was the perfect way to wrap up the story, ending the narrative on an ambiguous yet satisfying note that few dramas, modern or classic, can match. Yes, there were a few plausibility issues, such as with Daniel's testimony, and there are still some viewers out there who would have preferred the movie clarified if Sandra was guilty or innocent (depending on their interpretation). However, these camps are in the minority, and overall the end of Anatomy of a Fall was incredibly well received as a complex ending to an equally complex story.

While ambiguous endings can be a tricky thing to pull off, some movies, like Anatomy of a Fall, can leave lingering questions because the answer is not the point of the story. This is reminiscent of the ending of Inception, which leaves the audience with the iconic final shot of the top spinning, cutting to black before the audience knows for sure if Dom (Leonardo DiCaprio) is dreaming or awake. While the answer has been debated for years, the point is that Dom doesn't care anymore if this is real or not.

Anatomy of a Fall pulls off a similar ending. In fact, the movie is more effective with that fact left as a mystery. That is not to say audiences are meant to continue digging for clues, but rather they are being left with the same uncertainty the characters now have to live with.

Without having the answers as well, the audience is put in the same position as these characters in the final moments.

Anatomy of a Fall is not about the outcome of a murder trial, it is about these characters and what these accusations have done to their lives. If Sandra is guilty, she and Daniel have to live with knowing he lied to protect her. If she is innocent, she has to live with the knowledge that he might not believe she is innocent.

Without having the answers as well, the audience is put in the same position as these characters in the final moments. The ending of Anatomy of a Fall achieves a brilliant sensation of relief followed by the unnerving and sad reality of what comes next.

Anatomy of a Fall (2023) is a French courtroom drama about a writer accused of murdering her husband after he is found dead outside their isolated Alpine home. As the trial dissects their troubled marriage and forces their blind son to testify, the mystery becomes less about proving exactly what happened than about how imperfectly people can ever know one another. The film won the Palme d’Or at Cannes and the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay.

In fact, this is the most flexible underwear I’ve tested during my runs. Each piece is dyed in small batches, making every pair unique.

I’ve had a few of Skims’ Fits Everybody Dipped Front Thongs for years—it’s that good, I couldn’t just stop at one. Hands down, it’s the softest pair on this list. The On Gossamer thong is thinner and has more spandex, giving it a more compressive, workout-like feel. But this one is soft and stretchy without that snap, making it feel looser and more buttery. Despite its high polyester content, it has more of a cotton-like texture that’s super comfortable. I wouldn’t wear this underwear with tight leggings as it has a looser fit and it's not seamless, but this is my go-to underwear to wear with trousers, jeans, or sweats.

However, it’s still extremely breathable and quick drying, and kept us feeling cool and fresh during HIIT workouts. Unlike other thongs I own, this one never digs into my skin.This underwear also has a dipped front, which I prefer while wearing low-cut pants or crop tops. You never have to worry about it sticking up over your pants, as it doesn’t have a super high, thick band.The “Fits Everybody” line is my favorite that Skims offers, and there are so many different bras and underwear you can shop within this soft, stretchy line. There’s an Adaptive Thong, T-String Thong (another favorite of mine), and my go-to bra, the Fits Everybody Scoop Bralette.

In my opinion, every woman needs a good pair of boyshorts—for sleeping, extra coverage under short dresses, layering under jeans for warmth, or even wearing solo to yoga or Pilates. This pair from lululemon is perfect for all of that. It looks just like a pair of biker shorts (so no one will know it’s underwear!), but it has the breathability and moisture-wicking benefits of a great pair of undies.

This short is made from 91 percent modal (which is softer than cotton) and nine percent elastane for the perfect amount of stretch. It feels buttery soft, but the bit of spandex gives it a subtle snap, making it great for workouts or light compression under a dress. The flat seams stay invisible under clothes and help prevent chafing, while the smooth waistband sits comfortably without digging in or showing through.

This short has a five-inch inseam and a super high rise, making it a versatile fit for all kinds of outfits. In my opinion, it’s the perfect length for layering under clothes. When I wear it solo to a workout class, I wish it didn’t have stitching at the crotch—this makes it look more like underwear than workout shorts. But don’t get it twisted—I still wear it to the gym all the time. Plus, it’s moisture-wicking and quick drying, so I never have to worry about feeling damp down there after a sweaty sesh.

As a style writer, I test tons of underwear. For the original version of this story, written in 2023, I rounded up my all-time favorite pairs I’ve ever worn. Over the past three years, I’ve continued to put them through their paces (and tried even more options) to find only the best underwear for women.

In addition to speaking with fabric and feminine health experts about what to look for in a good pair of underwear, I tested each pair at the gym, around the house, on errand-running days, and on long days out and about to see which ones earned top marks across comfort, style, breathability, rise, fit, size options, and more. I wore and washed each pair multiple times, and rated them based on the following:

9 Best Winter Boots for Women, Tested and Reviewed by Fashion Editors

📅 2023-11-30  |  Read Source →

After years of testing, our top pick is from Sorel.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

As a style writer, I live in comfortable sneakers and heels for most of the year. But come winter, my favorite shoes can’t handle New York City’s slick, slushy streets. That’s when I swap in a tried-and-true waterproof winter boot. For the past two years, WH editors have been testing tons of cold-weather shoes and have found the best options that keep our feet warm without skimping on style.

During evaluations, we put a range of comfortable boots to the test, including chic leather options for warmer climates, warm hiking boots, and insulated styles for the chilliest locales. We wore them during long, snowy days on Finland’s slopes and wet morning commutes to our New York City office. The result? A curated guide to the absolute best options for different preferences and weather conditions.

What’s New: - At the close of last winter, we added The North Face Thermoball Lace Up Waterproof Boots to our guide. Dorenna Newton, executive producer for Men’s Health and Women’s Health, tested this boot in St. Moritz while covering Team USA’s bobsled training ahead of the Olympics. - In our November 2026 update, I added the Columbia Snowtrot Mid Boot and the Moon Boot Icon Low Pearly Plus after testing both pairs in Iceland. Both scored major style points, while the Snowtrot excelled in wet conditions and the Moon Boot won me over with its extreme warmth and comfort when temps plummeted.- The Columbia Minx Shorty IV Boot continues to prove its top-notch water resistance and warmth. This boot won me over in Finland last year, and I wore it nonstop during winter 2026 in NYC while navigating slushy streets and freezing temps.- We’re currently testing a handful of more winter boots as temperatures start to drop and will update our guide with the best new styles we find.

We were first drawn to the Sorel Caribou boot because its laces and colorways look more stylish than most other winter boots. But after testing it for over two years, we found it’s also warm enough to handle super-cold temps and repels water like a pro.

Starting with style, the quilted padding, metal hardware, and lace-up front closure add a nice design touch that separates this from other serious winter boots. It pairs well with jeans, leggings, or even a cool maxi skirt or dress. We love the orange color, but if that shade is a little too much for you, the brand also makes beige and black styles that pair well with any outfit.

These boots also have lugged soles for excellent traction and are insulated and waterproof to keep you warm and dry in serious weather conditions. The upper is made from high-quality leather with a seam-sealed construction to keep moisture out. Plus, they have a rubber mudguard at the toes for extra warmth and protection, and a removable synthetic liner so you can customize your level of insulation.

“The fit is secure, so nothing is getting through these babies,” says Saladino, who wears this for snowy weekdays in New York City and ski weekends. “They’re perfect for après-skiing, shoveling the driveway, or anytime you need complete and total protection from the elements,” she says.

Her only complaint? They are a little on the heavier side, weighing in at two pounds and one ounce.

This cozy boot is the perfect pull-on style for casual snowy days and quick outings, Saladino says. Case in point: it's ideal when you need to take the dog out or you’re jetting out the door for school drop-off. There’s also extra room inside the boot, which Saladino loves when she needs to slip it on and go.

Despite the short style, the weatherproof suede boot is plenty warm. The faux-fur lining adds a cozy layer of insulation. We also like how light it is, even though it has a thick rubber outsole that’s super grippy on slippery surfaces.

Plus, it has a clean, simple design and cozy-chic look that you’ll actually want to wear all winter long. We love the contrast between the suede upper and the lighter-colored outsole, and think this pair looks adorable styled with a pair of wool socks and leggings.

Our only word of warning is that because the shaft height on this boot is on the shorter side, it may not be ideal for extra snowy days. If you need a boot to handle more intense winter weather, we recommend opting for The North Face Shellista IV Mid WP.

On an October trip to Iceland, I opted for this waterproof pair, since fall there is super unpredictable and rainy. While I opted for hiking boots most of the time, the Columbia Snowtrot Boot proved its waterproof capabilities on a particularly wet day of the trip, not letting a drop of water inside the shoe.

Considering how warm it kept my feet, I know I’ll be reaching for these all winter in New York. I love the puffy silhouette with its quilted upper and the monochrome finish in the all black colorway (which looks way more streamlined than similar pairs I’ve seen with white or gum soles). It’s lightweight, easy to pack, and has a sleek look that styles well with leggings and a puffer jacket or sweater. I especially like that they don't have the bulky feel I’ve come to expect from a winter boot.

Where this boot really stands out is its weather protection. It’s made with multiple layers of breathable synthetic materials and reinforced seams that help keep rain and moisture out. It also has 200 grams of insulation and a soft fleece interior to keep feet warm and cozy.

I also appreciate the side zipper, which makes them easy to slip on and off (especially handy when putting on your boots while bending over in bulky pants and jackets). The rubber outsole also helps provide tons of traction on both wet and dry surfaces, with a grippy tread pattern that comes in handy while navigating rainy sidewalks, muddy paths, or icy ground.

While it costs a fraction of the price of other winter boots, Dream Pairs makes a solid winter shoe that keeps cold and wet weather out. In addition to a water-resistant faux leather, the shoe has a plush faux-fur interior that’s super insulating. It also has a 1.37-inch rubber anti-slip sole for better traction in slippery conditions. The sole has 2mm of plush memory foam for added comfort and shock absorption. We also appreciate the pull tab on the back of the boot, which makes them easier to slip on and off.

Like our top overall pick, we like that this winter boot comes in a variety of colors: beige, nude, light gray, chestnut, and black. The cozy faux-fur lining, monochromatic laces, side panel stitching, and sturdy sole make it super stylish and practical. It easily slips under snow and ski pants, and looks just as cute styled with a pair of leggings and fuzzy socks.

On the downside, our testers said they noticed signs of wear and tear sooner than other pairs, particularly ripping of the faux-fur lining.

When I started crafting my packing list for a recent trip to Northern Finland, a cute but snow-proof winter boot was at the top of my list. After lots of research, I landed on the Columbia Minx Shorty IV Boot—a perfect blend of style, traction, water resistance, and warmth.

The moment I slipped this boot on, I loved the cozy, faux-fur insulation that kept my feet warm even on frigid mornings and evenings. And the waterproof nylon outer meant I didn’t have to worry about slushy streets or fresh snow seeping through. The traction is also super impressive, and I felt comfortable walking over icy sidewalks, a frozen lake, and snowy trails.

The shaft height hits about two inches above the ankle, offering just the right amount of coverage for typical city snow or moderate winter adventures. While deeper snow might call for a taller boot, this pair provides the ideal balance between protection and mobility.

The cherry on top? It’s genuinely so stylish. The sleek design, color selection, and faux-fur collar mean you don’t have to sacrifice fashion for function. I’ve paired them with everything from fleece-lined leggings and Fair Isle sweaters, snow pants and a winter coat, and even jeans—and they always look great. It was my go-to boot for the whole trip, and I know I’ll get just as much use out of it this winter in New York.

If your feet are perpetually cold once winter hits, meet your new favorite snow boots. The boot features an extremely thick layer of insulation in the form of a cushioned foam lining that molds to your feet over time. Wearing this boot genuinely feels like stepping into a giant marshmallow. I especially like that the platforms lift your feet off the cold, wet ground, which makes a huge difference in keeping them toasty. Plus, the shearling details add a cozy touch.

I also love Moon Boot’s iconic, space-age silhouette with its oversized shape. The Italian brand has built a reputation for seriously chic après-ski style, but don't let the fashion-forward appearance fool you. The rubber tread outsole provides plenty of grip on snowy surfaces, while the surprisingly lightweight feel makes them comfortable for everyday winter outings, whether you're heading to the lodge or walking around town after a fresh snowfall.

Fun fact: These boots are ambidextrous, meaning there's no designated left or right boot, and they mold to your feet as you wear them (though I will say they feel really good straight out of the box).

After testing this boot in Iceland, I can say that having a genuinely warm, insulated pair of boots makes a big difference when you're outside in the cold for extended periods. This pair is hands-down my favorite option for especially frigid locations when warmth is your biggest priority, particularly if you're looking for something that doesn't sacrifice style.

Just note that the upper is water-repellent rather than fully waterproof, so I'd save them for snowy conditions rather than slushy streets or rainy days.

This boot scores major style points, whether you’re on the mountain or navigating slushy city streets. We love the nude tone (with a subtle sheen), horizontal stitching, and puffy silhouette. Toggle laces keep the look neat and polished, while branded pull loops on both sides add functional visual interest.

Dorenna Newton, executive producer for Men’s Health and Women’s Health, recently wore this boot in St. Moritz while covering Team USA’s bobsled training ahead of the Olympics. She loved that they looked “super chic” for après adventures in the village—earning style points along with practicality.

“I’m constantly on the move, so packing light is non-negotiable,” Newton says. “That means every item has to earn its place—including this brand-new pair of The North Face snow boots I decided to test in real time.” She says this boot delivered from the moment she slipped it on, feeling instantly comfortable while providing serious warmth on frigid mountainsides.

The shaft hits right above the ankle and delivers impressive warmth thanks to recycled polyester insulation and a cozy fleece lining. A drawcord cinches the boot at the ankle for added protection from cold air, snow, and rain. Paired with a durable, waterproof ripstop upper made from recycled water bottles, the boot fares well under any condition.

Like the The North Face Shellista IV, this boot has exceptional traction thanks to a grippy, rubber outsole, which Newton says kept her steady on icy ground. However, like our other pick from The North Face, this boot has a snug, rigid fit—so consider sizing up if you’re between sizes or have a wider foot.

We’re big fans of L.L. Bean’s iconic Duck Boot, and this fleece version is perfect for chilly weather. “I love the rugged weekend styling of this boot,” says Saladino. “It’s super cozy on the inside, and the fleece detailing and contrasting laces on the outside are cool styling touches.”

It’s also well-equipped for slushy snow, thanks to a waterproof leather upper to keep moisture out. Plus, it has a rubber outsole with a grooved tread pattern that helps you stay upright and balanced on slick sidewalks. Bonus: The boot is made with 200 grams of PrimaLoft insulation, an ultra-warm, quick-drying material to keep feet dry and toasty.

The brand doesn’t have half sizes, but we found it wise to size down if you’re between sizes. “I am a size 9, and it fits great even with a thick sock,” says Saladino. Overall, we were impressed by both style and function—particularly the traction, which makes it a bit more equipped for heavy winter conditions than other ankle-length styles.

The Ugg Classic Mini Platform is a well-loved classic, and freelance stylist Alexandra Juric says they're constantly in rotation during the fall and winter. It’s stylish, comfortable, and warm. It has that classic Ugg boot shape but with a trendy platform that gives total cool-girl vibes. But you'd better hurry up and *add to cart* if you want this style ahead of the holidays—it’s known to sell out quickly.

The inside of the boot is lined with the brand’s signature wool blend, which adds a fluffy layer of insulation and comfort. It also has a heavily cushioned EVA foam midsole that feels super plush under the foot. The suede outer adds to the cozy look and feel, though it’s less water-resistant than other leathers. We recommend snagging the shoe protector spray if you plan to wear them in wet weather. We also love that the added two-inch platform to the classic silhouette gives you height without sacrificing comfort or traction.

Associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian says this boot is the perfect addition to her winter wardrobe. "I've worn them on wet, rainy, snowy streets and they've stayed relatively clean, even in a lighter color," she says. "They're insanely comfortable with the plush interior, warm in even the coldest temps, and totally cradle my tired feet—I feel like I could walk miles in them!" She loves that they are super stylish and go with just about any outfit, but she's partial to styling them with a long trouser or flared leggings.

The downside? They don’t come in half sizes and tend to run big, so keep that in mind when shopping.

The type of boot you want for everyday city commuting is different from what you'd need for winter hiking or snowshoeing in seriously cold weather, says Julie Hardy, senior buyer at Zappos.

While a boot’s temperature ratings provide a useful starting point for what to look for when shopping, there's no one-size-fits-all rule, says Hardy. For most outdoor activities like snowshoeing, hiking, or backpacking, our experts suggest looking for a baseline of about 200 grams of insulation. Liners can also boost the product's warmth. Seam-sealed and waterproof features are also important if you spend a good amount of time in the snow or rain. Look for terms like "Thinsulate" and "GORE-TEX," both of which are trademarked materials that provide superior insulation.

Keep in mind that taller boots also help keep more of your leg warm even without the presence of snow. Generally, mid-height boots (about 6.5 inches) strike the perfect balance of coverage and comfort; however, tall heights (12 inches or more) are better suited for deep snow. Ultimately, shaft height is about personal preference, but make sure your boots go above the hem of your pants to keep snow and cold air out.

As a fashion writer who’s tried countless pairs of shoes over the past ten years, I know a thing or two about what makes a solid winter boot. I went to school in chilly upstate New York for four years, have a lifetime of NYC winters under my belt, and regularly travel to places with extreme conditions (most recently, Iceland and Finnish Lapland—above the Arctic Circle).

We first wrote this article in November 2023 with our team’s all-time favorite winter boots. But since we’re always testing new pairs each winter and during cold-weather vacations, I’m constantly updating the list with the absolute best winter boots from brands like Sorel, Columbia, Moon Boot, The North Face, Merrell, Ugg, and L.L. Bean.

I also consulted a senior buyer for Zappos, which is one of the largest footwear retailers out there, on what to consider when shopping for winter boots: materials, insulation, and shaft height. WH fashion contributors Kristin Saladino, Rose Lauture, Lily Wohlner, and freelance stylist Alexandra Juric also weighed in on their favorite options. Collectively, we have over 30 years of experience testing shoes and boots.
