Gift Guide: Best Tech and Gadgets for Gearheads and Car Lovers

📅 2023-11-10  |  Read Source →

Our car experts choose every product we feature. We may earn money from the links on this page.

Keep up with the latest automotive and garage tech with our picks for the best gadgets and tech on the market today.

This article was updated in November 2026.

Automotive enthusiasm has always gone hand in hand with a fascination for technology. At Road & Track, we’re always interested in the technology that makes the automotive experience better.

Some are practical necessities, others are just plain cool, but each has something to offer a car enthusiast. Think diagnostic scanners, GPS navigation systems, performance monitors, wireless phone accessories, and clever tools that help tackle jobs around the garage.

We’ve included options at various price points and for different kinds of enthusiasts, so you can find something useful, interesting, and worth keeping in the toolbox.

The Mission 1 Pro is built for capturing the kind of driving footage that makes you want to take the long way home. I recently used one myself on a drive up the Pacific Coast Highway, where its compact size made it easy to bring along and its high-resolution video captured everything from sweeping coastal views to the little details along the road. It’s a versatile action camera for car enthusiasts who want more than a few phone clips from their next road trip, with the rugged, portable design GoPro has built its reputation on.

The Cobra RAD 700i is less a radar detector and more a digital co-pilot for the fast lane. With long-range detection, GPS-powered AutoLearn filtering, and Bluetooth connectivity to Cobra’s Drive Smarter network, it helps cut through false alerts while keeping you tuned into live speed traps, cameras, and roadside hazards. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility sweeten the deal, turning your windshield into mission control for highway miles and heavy right feet.

A navigation app is only as useful as the cellular connection behind it, and that can become a problem once you get far enough outside town. The weBoost Drive X is a multi-user cellular signal booster that uses an external magnetic-mount antenna to capture available signals, then amplifies them for devices inside the cabin. Its amplifier delivers up to 50 dB of gain and supports several major U.S. cellular frequency bands. The kit includes both exterior and interior antennas, a power supply, and the amplifier itself, making it a worthwhile consideration for road trippers, overlanders, and anyone who regularly ventures beyond reliable cell coverage.

Running navigation, streaming music, and charging wirelessly can turn a smartphone into a little pocket-size space heater, especially on a summer road trip. Pioneer’s SDA-SC600 combines a magnetic Qi2 charging mount with an integrated cooling fan designed to help manage device temperatures during longer drives. It supports wireless charging at up to 15 watts, includes an adjustable air-vent mount, and uses a multicolor LED indicator to show charging status.

A phone running Google Maps isn’t going to cut it when the pavement ends and the trail network gets complicated. The Garmin Tread 2 Overland Edition is an eight-inch, glove-friendly GPS navigator built specifically for off-road travel, with preloaded topographic maps of North and South America, public-land information, and U.S. Forest Service Motor Vehicle Use Maps. Its IP67-rated enclosure is designed to withstand dust, water exposure, and rough conditions, while the included magnetic-assisted locking mount secures the unit to the dashboard. It also supports downloadable satellite imagery and route planning through Garmin’s Tread app, giving overlanders a much more capable navigation setup than a smartphone alone.

The BlueDriver Bluetooth Pro OBD2 Scanner is a compact diagnostic tool that plugs into a vehicle’s OBD-II port and sends information wirelessly to an iOS or Android device. Beyond reading and clearing standard check-engine codes, it offers enhanced diagnostics for systems such as ABS, airbags, transmission, and TPMS on supported vehicles. The companion app also provides live sensor data, Mode 6 test results, and repair reports with possible causes and reported fixes. With compatibility covering most 1996-and-newer North American vehicles and no subscription fees, it’s a useful step up from a basic code reader for anyone who likes doing their own troubleshooting.

A stopwatch can tell you whether your last lap was faster, but it won’t explain why. The Garmin Catalyst is a dedicated track-driving analysis system that combines a 10Hz multi-GNSS receiver, onboard accelerometers and gyroscopes, and an HD remote camera to record and evaluate a driver’s performance. Garmin’s True Track Positioning technology analyzes racing lines, braking points, apexes, and track-out positions, while its True Optimal Lap feature combines the best sections of recorded laps to show how much time is potentially left on the table. It can also deliver real-time audio coaching, making it a particularly interesting tool for track-day drivers who want to improve without investing in a complicated professional data-logging setup.

DJI’s Mini 4 Pro is packed full of impressive imaging capabilities and innovative navigation features. The 249-gram weight of the unit means the device is just under the Federal Aviation Administration’s 250-gram limit for registering your drone in the United States, significantly reducing the barriers to entry other drones require. The Mini 4 Pro captures 4K video at up to 100 frames per second (fps) or 4K at 60 fps with HDR video. The unit is rated for roughly 12 miles of transmission between the drone and the included remote, ensuring even congested areas or valleys/hills won’t impact your ability to record video or snap photos. Other features include 360-degree obstacle-avoidance sensors, a plethora of automated capture modes capable of locking in on and tracking subjects, and a 34-minute flight time with the included batteries.

Stop stuffing your pockets with multiple flashlights when you really just need this one. Holding the ArkPro Ultra feels immediately different than a standard flashlight; the flat, slim profile disappears in your pocket or EDC bag unlike bulky round tubes, yet the unibody aluminum feels incredibly dense and premium in the hand. It solves the biggest headache of carrying high-tech gear: charging anxiety. Because it finally supports both magnetic snap-charging and standard USB-C, you can top it off on your nightstand or with a laptop cable without hunting for a proprietary cord. Whether you are running a presentation or checking for leaks under a car, it feels like the Swiss Army knife of light that actually performs as well as the dedicated tools it replaces.

The IntelliDash Pro X10 is a modern shortcut for aging dashboards—a slim 10-inch touchscreen that brings wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto to just about any car without surgery, swearing, or a weekend in the garage. Setup is gloriously plug-and-play, with Bluetooth, FM, AUX, and voice-assistant support baked in. Big maps, brighter road trips, cleaner cable chaos. It’s the kind of upgrade that makes a 2009 commuter vehicle feel a little more spaceship.

A shiny new paint job can hide a lot of history, particularly on an older car that’s been through a few owners and at least one body shop. The Rdinscos Car Coating Thickness Meter is designed to measure the thickness of paint and other coatings on metal panels, giving buyers a way to compare readings across a vehicle’s bodywork. Uneven measurements can point toward previous refinishing, additional layers of paint, or body filler, making the tool particularly useful when inspecting a potential project or evaluating a used-car purchase. It’s not a replacement for a trained eye or a proper pre-purchase inspection, but it can help uncover evidence of repairs that a quick walkaround might miss.

The Hoto Tools Precision Screwdriver Kit Pro is a wonderful gift for any DIY aficionado or professional. The screwdriver uses a two-gear design to provide more than enough torque for delicate builds or repairs. It also features built-in LED lights and an innovative contact charging case that stores the drill and its accessories, ensuring power is always topped off when needed.

This kit isn’t just about looks—it’s about substance, with 48 bits forged from S2 steel, complemented by a suite of practical tools like spudgers, tweezers, and a suction cup for those tricky parts. The electric screwdriver’s adjustable torque and handy magnetizer/demagnetizer tool help to ensure no small bits and pieces go missing. Whether you’re a tech enthusiast or a creative tinkerer, the Hoto Tools kit provides practicality and precision in a compact, stylish package.

Built for gloveboxes, road trips, and “oh no” moments, the Vantrue JS3 is a compact four-in-one roadside powerhouse: jump starter, air compressor, fast-charging power bank, and emergency light, in one rugged shell. With a 3250-amp peak current, 160-psi inflator, and USB-C PD 65-watt charging, it’s designed to revive dead batteries, refill tires fast, and keep devices alive when the highway gets unpredictable. Think of it as roadside insurance with a lithium heartbeat.

Shopping for someone who already has every gadget is tough, but the Insta360 X6 is a guaranteed win. Because it shoots in every direction at once, you don’t even have to worry about framing—just hit record and pick the best angles later on your phone. The software automatically edits out the selfie stick, making it look like a low-flying drone is following you, whether you’re carving up back roads, hitting the mountain bike trails, or just messing around in the backyard. It’s incredibly easy to use and makes literally any activity look epic.

Reverse-engineering a custom intake manifold or replicating a classic car’s unobtainium trim pieces usually means dragging a fragile laptop into the grime of the garage. The Creality Sermoon P1 standalone 3-D scanner finally severs that tether. This isn’t some plastic hobbyist toy; it’s a high-octane engineering workstation crammed into a handheld chassis. Packing a Qualcomm 8-core processor and a massive 24GB of RAM, the P1 processes dense 3-D meshes directly on its crisp six-inch touchscreen. It boasts enough onboard horsepower to digitize a complete engine block without breaking a single drop of digital sweat. For the uncompromising gearhead looking to turn physical metal into flawless digital data, the Sermoon P1 is the ultimate garage weapon.

This cordless four-in-one Slim V8 Apex mini vacuum packs 19,000Pa suction into a glovebox-friendly frame, with attachments for crumbs, cupholders, keyboards, pet hair, and other chaos agents. It also blows, inflates, and pumps, making it equal parts detail tool and travel sidekick. Lightweight, USB-C rechargeable, and surprisingly mighty, it’s built for people who treat messes like pit stops—not permanent conditions.

The Nextmug Go is the kind of gadget that quietly upgrades your entire morning ritual. This sleek, self-heating travel mug keeps coffee or tea at your preferred temperature — Warm, Hot, or Piping — for hours, so every sip tastes freshly poured. Its spill-resistant lid, long-lasting battery, and app-free controls make it refreshingly simple to use on commutes, road trips, or marathon workdays. Think of it as a thermos with a master’s degree in modern convenience.

HoverAir’s X1 ProMax is the ultimate drone for people who don’t know anything about drones. This self-flying, fully enclosed camera launches from your hand and uses 10+ AI-powered shooting and follow modes to capture photographs and up to 8K/30 (or 4K/120) video, stabilized by SmoothCapture 2.0—a two-axis gimbal with electronic image stabilization (EIS) and horizon leveling. It’ll track confidently with a rated 42 km/h (26 mph) follow speed, and its OmniTerrain feature is designed for flying near water, snow, and other tricky surfaces. I’ve shot various drones over the years, and while others might be more technically capable, none are as simple to use as the ProMax. The best part is, it’ll fit nearly anywhere. It’s a no-brainer for anyone who wants to capture drone footage quickly in a device that folds up smaller than most books.

Ride1Up’s Revv 1 DRT is a moped-style e-bike that trades Lycra vibes for dirt-track energy. A 52-volt system feeds a 1000-watt Bafang rear hub and a 35-amp controller with a “boost” party trick, while a 52-vole/20-Ah UL-certified pack (about 1040 watt-hours) keeps the lights on. Off-road mode unlocks 28-plus mph for private property, and the chassis gets real hardware: a 150-mm dual-crown fork, 76 mm of rear travel, and flur-piston hydraulic stoppers. Range is quoted at 30–60 miles, and the whole package carries UL 2849/2271 safety certifications—welcome peace of mind on a 30-mph pseudo-moto.

On trail or torn-up alleys, the DRT feels like a small, electric pit bike: confident, quick to squirt, and more fun than it has any right to be. The flip side is familiar: short cranks and moped geometry make real pedaling an afterthought, knobby 20-by-fours hum and nibble at range, and you’ll want to mind local laws before touching that off-road setting. At $2395, it undercuts many fashion-forward rivals while delivering genuine off-road chops and useful kit (headlight fairing, molle mounting, twist throttle). If your commute occasionally turns to dirt, this is the hooligan commuter to beat.

Wolfbox’s G840S is the kind of upgrade that makes an older car feel quietly futuristic. This 12-inch smart-mirror dash cam layers 4K front recording, a rear backup camera, GPS tracking, parking assistance, and touchscreen controls into a sleek rearview mirror replacement. The wide-angle rear feed also helps tame blind spots—especially handy in crowded garages and tight parking decks. For drivers who want better visibility, accident protection, and cleaner tech integration without replacing the whole dash, it punches well above its weight.

Ballon d'Or 2027 Power Rankings

📅 2023-10-31  |  Read Source →

Harry Kane recently won the 2026 Ballon d'Or, but it's already time to look forward to what the next year of football will bring.

More importantly, who will be in contention for the prestigious individual prize in 12 months' time?

Much of that will hinge on which teams claim the biggest trophies, including league titles and the Champions League.

In the past, the prestigious individual accolade was based on the performance of players across a calendar year. However, the votes are now based on the results of the season.

Despite being a full year away from the 2027 ceremony, we've listed – and ranked – the players who are best placed to win the Ballon d'Or based on their respective teams' chances of success as well as their early-season form.

We've determined the order based on the following:

Desire Doue already looks like he's stepping up and becoming one of the most important players Luis Enrique has at PSG. With Bradley Barcola gone and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia absent for several months, the 21-year-old will be crucial.

He finished 14th in the 2025 Ballon d'Or and will be looking to improve on that next year. Having missed out on the 30 nominees in 2026, Doue has started the new season with eight goal contributions in 11 appearances for the French champions.

Will Ousmane Dembele regain the Ballon d'Or and join the exclusive club of players who have won the award more than once? If he can get back to the form that saw him crowned in 2025, there's every chance.

PSG are aiming for three Champions League titles in a row, and Dembele will now be vital to those plans with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia sidelined long-term. He's never been the most clinical in front of goal and only has four goals this season so far, but the France international brings pace, skill and technical ability to any team he plays for.

Is there a better all-action midfielder or set-piece maestro in world football right now? Except for his compatriot Jude Bellingham, the Arsenal and England star has no equal as things stand. Nobody is questioning that £100 million transfer fee now, following his big-money transfer from West Ham in 2023.

Rice inspired Arsenal to their first Premier League title since 2004 and was desperately hoping to follow that triumph with World Cup glory this summer. If he can repeat his form during the current season, he will reinforce his status as one of the world's best midfielders.

Erling Haaland is going to be under the microscope even more in the coming months. He'll need to block out the noise at Manchester City to continue his unbelievable form in front of goal.

The Norwegian became one of the most popular players in the world after taking the 2026 World Cup by storm. His big personality and inevitability make him a likeable footballer.

It's rare to see Man City or Norway play a game without Haaland finding the back of the net. That has continued into the 2026-27 season, as he's already on 14 goals for his club in all competitions.

England's first Ballon d'Or winner since Michael Owen in 2001, Harry Kane was crowned the world's best footballer in October 2026 after another magnificent year with Bayern Munich and England.

The England captain became his nation's top goalscorer in 2023, as well as reaching second place in the all-time Premier League scoring charts after scoring an incredible 213 times for Tottenham. His move to Bayern has been a roaring success to date, as he's managed to win back-to-back Bundesliga titles.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: In taking just 104 games to do so, Harry Kane became the fastest player this century to reach 100 goals for a club playing in one of Europe's top five leagues.

Kane looks set for another stellar campaign in 2026/27. He's already scored 10 times for Bayern Munich, with 10 assists as well, while he starred for England in the first international break of the season, hitting the back of the net six times in four matches, including braces against Croatia and the Czech Republic.

Jude Bellingham may have struggled to produce his best form for Real Madrid week in, week out last season, but the all-action midfielder re-announced himself on the biggest stage at the 2026 World Cup.

While that tournament won't be relevant for the 2027 Ballon d'Or, it proves Bellingham is capable of producing magic, while also possessing the 'clutch' gene. If Jose Mourinho can help him get back to his best consistently, the former Birmingham City youngster will be in contention for the biggest awards in 12 months' time.

He's started the 2026/27 campaign brilliantly. After an outstanding performance in England's 7-0 rout of Croatia in the Nations League, Roy Keane said that he could go on to become one of the greatest players ever.

Jude Bellingham for Real Madrid in 2026/27

Raphinha is one of the players who can feel most hard done by after being left out of the 2026 nominees altogether. The Brazilian has been brilliant for several years at Camp Nou, and has even transitioned into a new role seamlessly.

Having previously played on both flanks, the versatile forward has taken to the centre-forward role exceptionally well. Raphinha already has 15 La Liga goals to his name in 2026-27, and 19 in all competitions. His red-hot form makes him an early favourite for next year's award.

Michael Olise will certainly be in the mix if he keeps his breathtaking form up in 2027. The Frenchman broke the World Cup assists record in 2026, proving his worth as one of the best playmakers on the planet.

Having finished ninth in the voting for the 2026 award, Olise will be aiming for the podium at least next year. His cool demeanour allows the winger to remain composed in high-pressure situations. A skill many other Ballon d'Or winners have possessed.

Olise has started the 2026-27 season with a bang, earning Man of the Match as Bayern Munich beat Borussia Dortmund 2-1 in the German Super Cup. Weeks later, he earned another Man of the Match award after scoring two brilliant goals in Bayern's Champions League opener against Bodo/Glimt.

He also caught the eye with a hat-trick and two assists in a 7-0 league win over Union Berlin before scoring two superb goals in Zinedine Zidane's first two games as France boss.

Michael Olise for Bayern Munich in 2026/27

Kylian Mbappe has long been destined for the Ballon d'Or. The French forward has been touted as a future successor to Messi and Ronaldo, two of the greatest football players of all time – but now in his mid-20s, he's edging closer to cementing his status as the world's best footballer with an absurd amount of goals to his name season-on-season.

Mbappe, who scored 256 times for Paris Saint-Germain across 305 appearances, took a few months to get going at Real Madrid. But after finding the net 58 times for club and country in the 2025-26 season, there are few better finishers in world football. He already has double-figure goals in 2026–27.

Real Madrid have missed out on the biggest trophies in recent seasons, which has harmed Mbappe's chances at the biggest individual prize. If he can end his wait for Champions League glory, the sharp-shooting Frenchman will be at the front of the queue once again in 2027.

Despite narrowly missing out in 2026, Lamine Yamal could still become the youngest-ever winner of the award next year. His remarkable ability, combined with his superstardom, makes him something of a shoo-in in years to come.

Having already put one of the biggest clubs in Europe on his back since he was 15 and helped lead his country to a European Championship at 16, Yamal is clearly a fearless individual who embodies the phrase "if you're good enough, you're old enough."

After spending a season on loan at Barca, Marcus Rashford was blown away, calling Yamal his most talented teammate ever, before adding:

"If he ends up winning seven Ballon d'Ors, it wouldn't surprise me."

Barcelona's performance in the Champions League could play a big part in Yamal's fate. He's also started the 2026-27 campaign with Barcelona and Spain in scintillating form and is looking worthy of the Lionel Messi successor label. A

Bobby Flay Is Releasing A Pet Food Brand With His Cat Nacho

📅 2023-10-17  |  Read Source →

Food Network star Bobby Flay has a diverse professional portfolio. He’s hosted 17 different television shows, opened restaurants all over the country, and authored over a dozen cookbooks. His most recent venture, Made by Nacho, is the one closest to his heart. The chef founded his premium cat food brand in 2021 and named it after his beloved Maine Coon. Flay, a self-proclaimed “cat person,” would personally cook homemade meals for his cats Nacho and Stella.

He soon started offering his high quality recipes to pet owners around the world, tapping Nacho to be his unofficial business partner. Flay hasn’t been shy in showing his love for his pets, even bringing Nacho along to press appearances.

Nacho is understandably loved by fans—his own personal Instagram account has over 273,000 followers. The cat just celebrated his ninth birthday earlier this month and received well wishes from thousands of people. So it’s safe to say the public was devastated when Flay took to Instagram to share the tragic news of Nacho’s passing.

The chef, who largely shies away from sharing personal news with his fans, revealed that his heart is broken following the loss of his beloved pet. “I truly believe he was everyone’s cat in some way,” Flay wrote. “Nacho had a magic about him that was truly special.”

The loss of a family pet is never easy, but Flay says he’s soothed by “knowing his likeness and legacy will live on forever through Made by Nacho.” He ends the post by telling his fans to give his pets an “extra long hug today” and to send prayers to Nacho.

Flay’s post was quickly flooded with comments of support. Ina Garten wrote, “Oh Bobby I’m so sorry!! What a good life you gave him!!! 💔💔💔”

Fellow Food Network personalities Sunny Anderson and Aarti Sequeira also sent their love. “Love you, Bobby. Sending you all the love for sweet Nacho🧡,” Anderson said. Sequeira said, “I’m so sorry Bobby. Nacho brought out a different side of you that I love. Praying for comfort as you grieve.”

Fans who grew to love Nacho took to the comments section too, with one writing, “I am so sorry for your entire family. No matter how long our pets live, it’s never long enough.”

Sausage Stuffing Recipe

📅 2023-10-17  |  Read Source →

This sausage stuffing has everything you want on your Thanksgiving plate: crisp, craggy edges, a plush, savory center, and plenty of browned sausage throughout. Torn pieces of country-style bread soak up the broth and eggs without falling apart, turning golden and crunchy on top while staying tender underneath.

Breakfast sausage does much of the heavy lifting. Once browned, its drippings join plenty of butter to cook the onions, celery, and garlic. Fresh sage, parsley, and thyme bring balance, while optional fennel seeds add a little extra aromatic punch.

Uncooked pork breakfast sausage is the first choice. Typically seasoned with sage and black pepper, it brings familiar Thanksgiving flavors and plenty of richness. For some heat, choose spicy breakfast sausage. If you can't find the packaged kind or want to avoid pork, try making your own with our breakfast sausage recipe, using ground dark-meat turkey in place of pork.

This stuffing relies on the fat from breakfast sausage for its flavor. Want a vegetarian version? Our Simple-Is-Best Stuffing is a long-standing reader favorite and was the inspiration for this version; use that recipe with vegetable broth for a meat-free stuffing.

What’s the best bread for sausage stuffing?

Look for a sturdy country-style white loaf or sourdough with a relatively thin crust. Avoid soft sandwich bread, which can turn mushy, and very crusty artisan loaves, which won’t absorb the broth as readily. Even if your bread is a day or two old, don’t skip drying it in the oven—that’s what helps the stuffing hold its shape.

Can I make sausage stuffing ahead of time?

You can dry the bread a day ahead and store it loosely covered at room temperature. For more ways to get ahead of Thanksgiving, including cooking, refrigerating, and reheating stuffing, see our make-ahead stuffing guide.

Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 350°. Grease a 13x9" baking dish with unsalted butter. Arrange one 1–1¼-lb. loaf country-style white bread, torn into 1" pieces, in a single layer on a large rimmed baking sheet and bake until dried out and golden around the edges, 30–40 minutes. Let cool.

Meanwhile, melt 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high heat. Cook 1 lb. breakfast sausage, casings removed if needed, stirring and breaking into small pieces, until well browned and cooked through, 8–10 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer sausage to a small plate, leaving fat behind.

Reduce dial to medium heat and add remaining 8 Tbsp. unsalted butter to fat in pot; heat until melted. Cook 2 medium onions, finely chopped, 6 celery stalks, finely chopped, 8 garlic cloves, coarsely chopped, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. fennel seeds (if using), stirring occasionally, until onions are softened and golden around the edges, 12–15 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth along with sausage, ½ cup (packed) coarsely chopped parsley, 2 Tbsp. finely chopped sage, 2 Tbsp. finely chopped thyme, and ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper.

Whisk 3 large eggs and remaining 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth in a small bowl to combine, then stir into pot (don’t worry, eggs won’t scramble). Add bread to pot and toss gently to combine. Let sit, tossing occasionally, until liquid is almost completely absorbed, about 10 minutes.

Transfer stuffing to prepared dish (don’t pack or press down) and cover loosely with foil. Place dish on a clean large rimmed baking sheet and bake until stuffing is hot throughout (an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should register 160°), 35–45 minutes. Increase oven temperature to 400° and remove foil (no need to remove stuffing from oven while heat increases). Continue to bake until stuffing is light golden brown on top, 25–30 minutes longer.

Do Ahead: Bread can be baked 1 day ahead; store loosely covered at room temperature. Stuffing can be assembled 1 day ahead; cover and chill. Bring to room temperature before baking.

Editor’s note: This sausage stuffing recipe was first printed in our November 2023 issue; it has been updated for style. Head this way for more of our favorite Thanksgiving side dishes →

25 Best Defenders in World Football Right Now (Ranked)

📅 2023-10-09  |  Read Source →

A strong defender is vitally important to any successful football team. Sorting out the back-line is crucial, and having some serious defensive talent is a surefire way to build a team destined for silverware. Much focus is placed on attacking players, which is why any list of the best footballers in the world will always be dominated by that type of star.

However, we've highlighted the best defenders in the world right now, in order to give them their flowers for a change. From buccaneering full-backs to commanding centre-halves, the beautiful game is laced with talented defenders in all shapes and sizes. Here are the best players who operate at the back in a role that has been unsung for too long.

Given that trying to separate those on the list is such a difficult task, a number of factors will be taken into consideration as to where they end up in the rankings. These include:

The imposing France international is a great example of the modern centre back: athletic, composed, and complete with impressive attributes that exceed his defensive capabilities. Dayot Upamecano built a formidable duo alongside Ibrahima Konaté at RB Leipzig, leading both to the French national team and transfers to elite European teams.

Upamecano has established himself as a key part of Bayern Munich's defensive setup, securing several league titles and domestic cup triumphs since his move in 2021. With France, Upamecano has featured regularly, winning the Nations League in 2021 and playing the entire 120 minutes of France's World Cup final loss to Argentina in 2022. In 2026, he was one of nine defenders to be nominated for the Ballon d'Or.

Luka Vuskovic has been a revelation since joining Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2026. The Croatian has been tipped for great things since a loan spell at Hamburg put him on the Seagulls' radar in the first place. Tottenham Hotspur still decided to sell up, however, cashing in for as much as £50m.

Known for his aerial ability, recovery pace and modern passing range, the young defender is already among the very best in his position. The future is certainly bright.

Marc Guehi has been a fine defender for a number of years now but has really established himself at the highest level over the past three seasons.

He performed well for England at Euro 2024, as they made it to the final of the tournament, losing to Spain. He then followed that up by captaining Crystal Palace to their first-ever major trophy, as they defeated Liverpool in the FA Cup final, before beating them again to win the Community Shield a few months later.

Guehi earned a big move to Manchester City in 2026 after a 2025 summer move to Liverpool fell through. The England man has since established himself at the heart of the defence, helping the club to win the FA Cup during the 2025/26 season.

Alphonso Davies has been one of the most exciting attacking fullbacks in football for some time now, really breaking into the Bayern Munich team during the 2019/20 season, in which he helped deliver a treble – made up of the Champions League, Bundesliga and the DFB-Pokal.

In total, he has seven league titles under his belt in Germany and has enjoyed a great deal of success with Bayern. The only issue has been fitness problems, as injuries have regularly interrupted his momentum in Munich. Davies will hope to keep himself fit if he wants to move higher up this list.

Riccardo Calafiori has quickly become one of the best defenders in the world. Swapping centre-back for a fullback role at Arsenal, the Italian has often provided a surprise goalscoring threat, combining his instinct inside one area with his defensive prowess in the other. He is among the most undroppable players under Mikel Arteta.

Injuries have threatened to delay his progress, but Calafiori still played a key role as Arsenal finally ended their wait for another Premier League title in the 2025/26 campaign.

While AC Milan are counting their lucky stars that they took a punt on Theo Hernandez’s signature in the summer of 2019, it’s his previous employers, Real Madrid, who will be kicking themselves for letting him go for such a paltry fee. Since moving from Spain to Italy, most fans would agree that Hernandez consistently ranks among the world's best defenders every season.

From Essien to Kaka, here are the 10 greatest players who have played for Real Madrid and AC Milan.

Quick enough to burst forward with ease, while his high IQ allows him to marshal the back line from the left-back berth, the Frenchman has every tool to play at the top level of the sport for the next decade or so. However, a recent move to Al-Hilal may make it difficult for him to keep his place in this list without regularly playing in Europe.

Marc Cucurella has undergone what many would consider to be somewhat of a redemption arc in the last couple of years. At Brighton, he was lauded as one of the best left-backs in the Premier League before his 2022 move to Chelsea led to a decline in form as he came close to being kicked out of Stamford Bridge within a year of his arrival.

What seemed to catapult him back into better form was Spain’s Euro 2024 victory. From that point, the full-back regained his confidence and mojo and, as a result, became an incredibly valuable member of both Chelsea and Spain's squads. After winning the 2026 World Cup with Spain, Cucurella earned a huge move to Real Madrid during the 2026 summer transfer window.

Over the course of the last 24 months, Willian Pacho has transitioned from a young defender looking to show his worth in European football to a winner of the continent’s biggest competition and one of its most highly touted defenders.

The Ecuadorian, who made a name for himself in Belgium and Germany before his big-money move to the French capital in 2024, has settled in at the Stade de France incredibly well. Linking up with the likes of veteran Marquinhos, he has excelled thus far as part of the back-to-back Champions League-winning squad. The future continues to look bright for Pacho.

When Abdukodir Khusanov's header allowed Chelsea to open the scoring just three minutes into his Manchester City debut, many predicted that it would be the defining moment of his Man City career for all the wrong reasons. Since then, however, he has been among the best defenders in the world.

The young centre-back is among the quickest in his position in the Premier League, if not the world, and uses that recovery pace to his advantage. Despite his age and relatively small stature, Khusanov also has no trouble when asked to outmatch opposition forwards on a physical level - winning 60% of his duels in the 2025/26 campaign.

There were some doubts over Ezri Konsa's ability to step up for a side like Arsenal. Those doubts couldn't have been put to bed any quicker if he tried, however.

The England defender has taken a seat at the top table and has not looked back since, having also won the Europa League with Aston Villa in the 2025/26 campaign. At the start of the 2026/27 season, he ensured that the Gunners didn't miss William Saliba during his absence for a single second.

It's worth noting that Konsa is also an England mainstay these days. The centre-back has earned his place for the Three Lions and could be crucial if they are to finally end their wai for silverware.

Ariana Grande’s Flipped Bob Is Fall’s Sweetest Trend

📅 2023-09-25  |  Read Source →

Late last month, Ariana Grande sent shockwaves around the beauty world with a single selfie. The singer, actor, and beauty brand founder had recently gone back to brunette, officially ending her Wicked era. Now, she took it a step further by chopping off her hair.

“After being blonde for so long, her ends were ready to go,” hairstylist Brandon Pietsch tells Vogue of the transformation. Grande’s golden metamorphasis for the role of Glinda in Wicked took place in 2022, and anybody who has dyed their hair for an extended period time knows the toll repeated chemical damage has on hair. So that’s where Pietsch’s shears came in. “This is all her real hair! Ariana’s hair was quite long, I’d say we took a good six inches off. The concept was a soft bob that was short enough to force her to take a break from the pony, paired with a rich, warm color closer to her natural shade. I'm personally obsessed with how the warm shade brings out the dark amber tones in her eyes.”

In the days since, she’s been (mostly) wearing in a singular style: The flipped-out bob. “Retro looks are coming back for fall in full force,” Pietsch says. He describes Grande’s haircut as a soft blunt bob with internal layers that allow her to style in a a variety of ways. With this chop, he also took her a touch closer to her natural shade of brunette. Perhaps her new signature look is brewing?

Grande isn’t the only celebrity going in on the flipped-out bob. Margot Robbie styled her hair in a similar way—with a return of the side bang!—for the Chanel Cruise show that took place in Australia on November 5th. The look, done by her go-to hairstylist Bryce Scarlett, was a sweet take on her somewhat-new blunt bob (and that cut came hot on the heels of the end of her Wuthering Heights tour, are we starting to see a pattern?). French girl extraordinaire Lea Seydoux and Ayo Edebiri have also taken their hair to new degrees with flipped ends.

What makes the look modern and not Stepford Wives is all in the prep and maintenance, according to Pietsch. “Bobs can actually be pretty high maintenance,” he says. Grande and company are wearing their flipped-bobs without a ton of volume at the crown (that was Jackie O’s signature style), but instead close to the head and at a precise angle. “For fall and winter, I'm loving softer, less blunt bobs with internal layering so the hair still has movement. Very ’60s, ’70s and ’90s.”

Certificates of Deposit (CDs) work similarly to online savings accounts or money market accounts in terms of offering great returns with zero risk. The difference is, CDs “lock your money up” for a specified period of time. To access your funds before the term ends, you’ll have to pay a penalty.

Although CDs offer less liquidity than a regular checking account or savings account, you might get a higher rate of return with this financial product. This is especially true if you open a CD account with a longer timeline; for example, a 60-month CD instead of a 12-month CD.

According to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), national average CD rates range from 0.23% to 1.81% depending on the CD term, as of writing.

However, quite a few banks offer vastly superior CD rates to consumers who do their research. We compared dozens of banks and financial institutions to find the best CD rates today. If you’re on the hunt for a high-yield CD, start your search here.

If your goal is securing a superior short-term investment, the best CD rates are worth exploring. To help in your search, we compared many of the top financial institutions and online banks to find options with the most attractive rates and terms.

Explore and contrast the top certificates of deposit (CDs) rates based on the highest Annual Percentage Yield (APY), spanning various terms including 3-month, 6-month, 1-year, 2-year, and 5-year options.

There are a few factors to consider when choosing where to open a certificate of deposit. These include whether you want to open your CD in person or online, the rates and terms that apply, and the fees required to access your money early.

The following reviews explain the CD rates for each of the top banks we profile and other details you should know.

PNC Bank offers a variety of popular banking products, including certificates of deposit. Its CDs don’t require any monthly maintenance fees, and you can monitor your account at any time online or with the BBVA mobile banking app.

CD terms range from 7 days to up to 10 years, and CDs with longer timelines pay higher CD rates. Note that penalties apply if you access your money early.

If you cash out your CD early, with a term of one year or less, you’ll pay $25 plus 1% of the amount withdrawn. If you cash out a CD with a longer-term early, you’ll pay $25 plus 3% of the amount you cash out.

CD Rates: Online CDs with terms from 11 months to 36 months currently pay up to 5.04% APY.

CIT Bank is known for its popular high-yield savings account, known as Savings Builder, but it also offers an array of CDs with excellent terms. Its 11-month, no-penalty CD stands out since it offers an excellent return rate. There are also no penalties if you need to access your money early.

CIT Bank also offers term CDs with various other lengths, as well as jumbo CDs for deposits of $100,000 or more. None of its CDs come with account opening fees or account maintenance fees.

CD Rates: CIT Bank currently pays from 0.30% to 3.50% APY on their CDs, depending on the term you choose. Top rates are offered on their 18 month CDs, which pay out 3.00% APY, respectively. With Discover, you can open a CD that lasts anywhere from three months to 120 months. There are no fees to open a CD, including account opening fees or maintenance fees.

Discover also stands out due to the reasonable penalties it charges if you need to access your money early. CDs with a term of less than one year, incur a penalty at three months of simple interest. Marcus by Goldman Sachs is a popular online bank for personal loans and high-yield savings accounts, yet it also offers rewarding CDs. Terms for its CDs range from seven months to six years, with a minimum $500 deposit to get started.

Marcus by Goldman Sachs even offers a 10-day guarantee that says you can move your rate up if the advertised rates on the CD you purchased increase within 10 days.

CD Rates: Some of the best CD rates from Marcus by Goldman Sachs are for its 9-month CDs, which currently pay 4.30% APY. Marcus by Goldman Sachs also offers limited-time CD rate promotions, like 4.40% on an 18-month CD.

Dry Brushing: Why I Do It Every Day And All The Benefits

📅 2023-09-13  |  Read Source →

It seems like every time I watch a get-ready-with-me video, the first step of the routine is dry brushing. And while I’ve tried it here and there, I never found myself committing to the act. But this skin-care practice is beloved by not only the likes of Gwyneth Paltrow and Tracee Ellis Ross, but also by functional health doctors and medical professionals as well.

So what is dry brushing? It’s the act of running a bristled brush across your skin while working against gravity (so working toward your torso on limbs) to help with moving the body’s lymphatic system.

Everybody raves about the myriad of health benefits that comes along with dry brushing—from physically exfoliating your skin and eliminating strawberry skin to increasing blood flow and potentially diminishing the appearance of circulation.

Perhaps, then, it’s time to really give it a try.

True to its name, dry brushing involves running a bristled brush over dry skin, most commonly on the body (though occasionally, on the face if you’re working with a face-specific brush that’s much softer). “It is a powerful Ayurvedic practice that both exfoliates the skin and opens detox pathways to support lymphatic drainage and boost immunity,” says Lauren Berlingeri, co-founder of HigherDose.

A simple pre-shower ritual, it isn’t just used in Ayurvedic medicine to stimulate the skin and the body’s lymphatic system, but in traditional Chinese medicine (a.k.a. TCM) too. It’s a practice that has stood the test of time, which is always a good sign when trying to understand whether a wellness “trend” is really worth its salt.

As well as stimulating lymphatic drainage, which helps in detoxifying the body, dry brushing is supposed to be effective for removing dead skin cells to smooth skin, boosting blood circulation, and reducing puffiness and water retention. It is a great way to invigorate body and mind, especially at the start of the day. And some say it’s also great at reducing the appearance of cellulite, but from my personal research, this seems somewhat unfounded.

Sophie Bolvary, licensed massage therapist at Sanara, adds that the practice of dry brushing may boost our immune system: “The lymphatic system does not have a ‘pump’ of its own, meaning it only gets working when we start moving our body or when it is stimulated manually by dry brushing or light massage,” she explains.

She adds that different brushes can have a different effect on the body. Dry brushes made with boar-hair bristles are ideal for daily use and exfoliation. Dry brushes with ionic-copper bristles carry the added benefit of sweeping your body in negative ions, which is known for antiviral and antibacterial properties in traditional medicine. It also may bring us full body-mind refreshment as an added self-care benefit.

“The brisk rhythmic motion creates a sensory reset that I find both grounding and energizing,” Bolvary adds. “Helping to sharpen mental alertness and brighten my mood.” Pro tip: Sprinkle an essential-oil blend (like something with citrus) to your dry brush to further wake up your senses.

I’ve used a dry body brush during episodic health kicks previously, but rarely consistently—but my coworker swears by it before every shower, especially when she’s taking an “Everything Shower.” What I’ve most noticed since making it (at least) a four-times-a-week thing is that my skin is infinitely looking more polished and brighter. It’s an excellent way to quickly slough off the dead skin cells that form a grey veil over what was months before a summer tan, and it’s certainly a good way to wake yourself up in the morning.

I have found that combining it with a “contrast” shower—i.e., turning the temperature hot, then cold, then hot, then cold—makes me feel extremely energized, particularly after a vigorous workout. You also don’t really need to commit to doing five minutes to reap the benefits—give it three minutes and you’ll feel fantastic as you start your day. It’s worth noting that—as hard as I willed it—dry brushing won’t stimulate lymphatic drainage enough to cure a hangover. This is deeply disappointing, but I continue to search for a fix.

Newbies to the practice should know that once you’ve dry-brushed, you’ll likely experience an itchy, tingling sensation, along with some possible redness, which soon settles. This feeling quickly becomes less prominent with regular use, but it’s actually a sign that your circulation is revved up and blood is en route to the surface of the skin.

You also might feel, for lack of a better way to phrase it, like your skin is dusty. This is all the dead skin cells you just exfoliated off—which is why most people prefer to do this practice before hopping in the shower. Don’t fret, a little big of your favorite body soap will take care of it.

Dry body brushing is a really easy—and affordable—ritual to commit to, which is why it gets a yes from me. You can’t always see the many benefits it has on the body, but you can often feel them. I have personally noticed a more even skin tone, slightly lighter-feeling legs (not yet as streamlined as Paltrow’s, unfortunately), and more morning vitality. I also firmly believe that taking a few intentional minutes to do something positive for your well-being each day is underrated.

Next up… time to crack body moisturizing. A look at the dry brushes we’d recommend, below.

There are a few negative side effects that can occur if you’re not careful. Marisa Garshick, MD, board-certified dermatologist at MDCS Dermatology, says that it may cause irritation or micro-tears in the skin if too much pressure is applied. You’ll also want to consider what skin conditions you might be dealing with and if your skin type can tolerate all this brushing. Dr. Garshick says it’s not recommended for anyone with sensitive, broken, or inflamed skin like eczema or psoriasis.

Bolvary adds that you’ll want to be mindful about cleaning your brush (more on how to do that later). Because of the exfoliating nature of dry brushing, there could be a lot of skin-shedding debris that builds up in the brush that can make dry brushing ineffective or irritate your skin further.

Dr. Garshick says that dry brushing can be done one to two times a week if you have sensitive skin, as frequent brushing might cause irritation. But if your skin can tolerate it, Bolvary says that it can be a daily practice. She recommends doing it at the start of your day, right before hopping in the shower. “Some people find it more stimulating and energizing than a cup of coffee,” she says. Here’s to hoping.

Dry brushing done by a professional will give you a more in-depth treatment. “The practitioner takes care of the work, and reaches all the hard-to-reach areas, while you simply enjoy the awakening sensations,” says Bolvary. “Also, the practitioner can demonstrate proper technique and pressure for your skin and body type.”

But that doesn’t mean doing it at home won’t have its own benefits. She says it’s helpful to look at a lymphatic glow map: “A very easy Google search, which can outline the general flow of lymph and how to sweep into the main lymph ports of the body.” After a few tries on your own, she says, you get used to it.

Bolvary says that because dry brushes are usually made with natural materials, it’s best to use natural, non-chemical cleaning solutions to clean your brushes. “I like to get a bowl of warm water with several drops of tea tree oil and place the brush bristles down to let it soak for about 30 minutes. Then set it aside to dry.”

But keep in mind that your brush will soften over time and will eventually shed a little with regular washing. “These tools are not meant to last forever,” she says. “So if your brush has become too soft and the bristles are falling out with every use, it may be time for a new one.”

Try to wash your brush once every two weeks and spritz it with something like tea tree mist after every use. Bolvary also recommends leaving it in a window to air-dry rather than on your shower ledge, where it can easily get dirty.

When we test and review a product, we take a holistic approach to deliver well-rounded product recommendations. First, we lean on Vogue’s vast network of experts—from board-certified dermatologists to celebrity estheticians—to gain professional acumen on the industry’s standout products, ones these specialists would actually use on their clients. We pair their expertise with our editorial best practices to curate the thoughtful edits you read on our site.

As it relates to dry brushes, we selected the best based on the following characteristics: bristle type, texture, handle length, size, and the skin and wellness concerns they address. Rob is senior football editor at GiveMeSport, with over 15 years experience covering sport in various capacities since graduating from the University of Gloucestershire in 2008 with a degree in journalism. A childhood obsession for all things football developed into a career writing about the beautiful game, initially producing content for clients including Luton Town Football Club and the PGMOL. His first big interviews were with Premier League referees Howard Webb and Michael Oliver in 2009. He then spent four years producing written content for a betting website, mainly focusing on football, and was there to cover various games and tournaments including the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012. Rob joined GiveMeSport in 2013 (initially as a sub-editor before becoming a senior writer and then senior editor in 2020) and has covered countless football matches and other sporting events, interviewed various high-profile figures including Rio Ferdinand, Peter Crouch and Theo Walcott, and written well over 10,000 articles during that time. Rob has played a key role in GiveMeSport's coverage of the World Cups in 2014, 2018 and 2022, plus Euro 2016, Euro 2020 and Euro 2024, along with many Champions League finals. While football is Rob's area of expertise, he has also covered a wide range of other sports during his time at GiveMeSport including boxing, tennis and darts, as well as the 2016, 2020 and 2024 Olympic Games.

Not many Manchester United supporters will look back at Ralf Rangnick’s time at the helm fondly, though he did all he could to set the club up for a more prominent future. The 68-year-old German, who is currently in charge of the Austrian national team, was appointed the Red Devils’ manager on an interim basis in November 2021 - but ultimately failed to prove his worth.

He was poised to remain at the club in a consultancy role to support Erik ten Hag in his inaugural season in England, but upped and left soon after the Dutchman’s arrival. Rangnick, who has registered the worst points-per-game ratio of all managers to have attempted to steady the ship after Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement (with the exception of Ruben Amorim), took charge of all recruitment-based decisions at RB Leipzig and Red Bull Salzburg but failed to stamp his authority in Manchester in the same regard.

There were, however, a flurry of names that he recommended to the club during his short association, though none of them came to fruition. "Open-heart surgery" is what Rangnick claimed the squad needed during his final weeks at the club, as he made it clear that significant changes were required – and some time down the line, it’s evidently clear that the same issues are still embroiled at Old Trafford.

According to the Daily Mail, there were several names discussed as potential signings by Rangnick, including Manchester City duo Josko Gvardiol and Erling Haaland. But that’s not where the list ends. Some have made alternative high-profile moves, and some are still waiting to be snapped up. Let’s take a look at what they’re all up to now.

Enzo Fernandez is now playing for the blue half of Manchester after joining City from Chelsea for a joint-British record fee of £125 million in the summer.

The 25-year-old played a limited number of games for Benfica before making the move to England in 2023 and showed glimpses of his world-class qualities during his time at Stamford Bridge.

On the international stage, Fernandez was a key part of Lionel Scaloni’s 2022 World Cup-winning squad - even if it was Lionel Messi, one of the greatest football players of all time, who deservedly dominated the headlines during and after the tournament in Qatar. Even prior to that, though, United were reportedly keeping a close eye on the midfielder while he was at River Plate.

However, it's understood that the club were waiting for incoming manager Erik ten Hag to give the green light before signing him. The one (slight) silver lining is that his arrival may have stunted the development of England's Kobbie Mainoo, who has shown that he has the potential to become a top player for club and country - even if things didn't go to plan for him under Ruben Amorim.

United’s local rivals Manchester City are the Premier League club that took a calculated punt on the highly-rated defender. Despite his tender age, Josko Gvardiol starred for Croatia during the 2022 World Cup and rightfully earned praise and, in turn, his big-money move.

The 24-year-old was a domineering asset for his previous club, RB Leipzig, playing 87 games during his stint in Germany. After a shaky start to life in England, he has taken his game to new heights under the stewardship of Pep Guardiola. Given United's continued issues with Luke Shaw, a left-back of this quality going begging is one they may live to regret.

Despite playing second-fiddle to Erling Haaland during his Manchester City stint, Julian Alvarez is now widely regarded as one of the world's best forwards and deservedly so. He caught the eye of various top clubs while playing for River Plate in his native Argentina after notching 85 goal contributions in 122 games and transferred much of that form over to the Etihad Stadium.

Had United acted on Rangnick's advice, though, Alvarez might have been playing for the red side of Manchester instead. Rangnick was reportedly furious when the club failed to secure the Argentine's signature before he signed for City. After 36 goals in 103 appearances for the Sky Blues, he completed an £81 million switch to Atletico Madrid, where he managed to score an impressive 29 goals in his first season with the Spanish club.

Alvarez attempted to force a move to Barcelona in the summer but remains an Atletico player... for now.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Julian Alvarez became the first player in football history to win the Treble and the World Cup in the same season.

Luis Diaz's spell at Liverpool was largely positive, albeit marred ever-so-slightly by inconsistency at times. In his brightest moments, though, the livewire forward was truly electrifying. He haunted the Red Devils on numerous occasions as he has managed five goal contributions in six clashes, with a double coming during the Merseyside club's 3-0 victory at Old Trafford in September 2024. He made the move to Bayern Munich last summer and has hit the ground running in Germany.

Before becoming Jurgen Klopp’s marquee winter signing in 2022, the dynamic Colombian international was one of FC Porto’s driving forces, scoring 41 goals and registering 19 assists for the Portuguese heavyweights - so it’s no wonder that Rangnick had his eye on him. United's loss was undoubtedly Liverpool's gain, as he helped the Reds win a Premier League title.

Of all the missed opportunities, this one will sting the most for the Old Trafford faithful. Erling Haaland has been nothing short of extraordinary for Manchester City following his arrival from Borussia Dortmund. United legend Wayne Rooney even described him as the world's best footballer now that the Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo era has come to an end.

The goal-machine needed just 105 games to score his first 100 Premier League goals, and his links to Old Trafford go even further back than Rangnick's desperate plea. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer confirmed that the domineering forward was a man that the former United boss had told the club to sign long before he took the job in 2018.

As the 2021-22 season came to a close, it was patently clear that reinforcements in midfield were desperately needed at Old Trafford - hence why Konrad Laimer was eyed. At that time, the versatile midfielder had also caught the attention of Bayern Munich, who he eventually signed for, but Manchester United could have saved themselves money and hassle if they elected to sign him back when Rangnick first recommended the Austrian to the club’s higher-ups.

At Bayern, Laimer is a solid rotational option who would likely settle in well at Old Trafford, much like his former teammate Marcel Sabitzer did during his loan spell. Rangnick did at least get the chance to coach the midfielder, as he is a key part of the Austrian national team.

Alvaro Morata, 33, is somewhat of a footballing journeyman, having plied his trade for Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid, Juventus and Chelsea - though he has never quite managed to establish himself as one of Europe’s elite strikers. The Spaniard has scored goals wherever he's played during his career, although profligacy in some of the biggest fixtures has prevented him from establishing a reputation as a truly world-class forward.

The Spaniard was initially linked with a move to the Theatre of Dreams in 2017, but United opted for Romelu Lukaku instead. In the years since Rangnick's recommendation, the pressing-forward led Spain to European glory and sealed a move back to Italy, this time to multi-time Champions League winners, AC Milan. He quickly fell out of favour at the Serie A giants, though, and was shipped out on loan to Como at the beginning of the 2025/26 season.

Morata is now playing for Leganes, on loan from Como, in the second tier of Spanish football. File this one under 'bullet dodged', perhaps.

Christopher Nkunku could have become Manchester United’s first signing of the Ten Hag era after being one of RB Leipzig’s most notable stars. The Frenchman had a plethora of big-name clubs vying for his signature as he spearheaded Leipzig to a top-four finish in back-to-back seasons between 2021 and 2023, scoring a respectable total of 70 goals during his time at the club.

Injuries plagued the forward during his ill-fated spell with Chelsea, which left him determined to resurrect his career in Serie A. He scored eight goals in 35 games for Milan last season but is now back on loan with RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga.

Christopher Nkunku scored his third Premier League goal of the season as Chelsea beat Brighton at the Amex Stadium.

Imposing centre-forward Dusan Vlahovic, who was tipped to become a star on football's biggest stages, could have been a Manchester United player had the club been keen to listen more to Rangnick's transfer advice. Currently plying his trade in Turkey for Besiktas, the 26-year-old was previously one of Serie A's most recognisable forwards, despite struggling to show the same potency as he did during his time at Fiorentina.

Once on Arsenal's radar, there's still a chance that fans will get to see Vlahovic in the Premier League one day. But for now he's focused on scoring goals in the Turkish Super Lig.

All statistics courtesy of Transfermarkt - accurate as of 10/11/2026.
